data.title: Launch HN: Gecko Security (YC F24) – AI That Finds Vulnerabilities in Code
data.author: jjjutla
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个代码漏洞扫描工具的评价与讨论

不同观点：
• **关于写入权限的担忧**：
  - [physix] 和 [Retr0id] 提到工具要求GitHub登录权限，包括写入个人资料，他们质疑为什么一个漏洞扫描工具需要这样的权限。
  - [Retr0id] 明确表示不愿意为了漏洞扫描授予“代表我行事”的权限。

• **工具的有效性评价**：
  - [hayali] 认为工具是“AI炒作”，并指出其对开源项目的假设（都托管在GitHub/GitLab上）不准确，且扫描结果（如发现IRC脚本漏洞）被认为不实用或可笑。
  - [skanga] 使用工具扫描自己的项目后未发现任何漏洞，开始质疑是自己的代码完美还是工具存在问题。
  - [bearsyankees] 提到工具给出了不真实的漏洞警告，并质疑其“100%信心”的依据。

• **工具的技术讨论**：
  - [pns1] 对工具如何处理动态语言（如JavaScript、TypeScript）的调用图表示好奇，并询问了如何将动态类型信息存储到Protobuf中，同时关心上下文信息对漏洞检测的帮助。
  - [dnsbty] 认为LLM（大型语言模型）在代码安全分析领域有很大潜力，但目前的静态分析工具效果有限，希望工具能够提供更具上下文的扫描。

• **工具的UI与错误处理问题**：
  - [mdaniel] 提到工具的UI错误提示不明显，认为安全工具不应在错误处理上马虎。

• **与竞争对手的比较**：
  - [eranation] 询问工具与Corgea.com以及其他通用AI代码审查工具（如Cursor BugBot、GitHub Copilot Code Reviews、CodeRabbit）的区别。

• **工具的使用建议与潜在问题**：
  - [hajrice] 建议工具可以扫描拥有大量关注者的GitHub项目以吸引用户注意。
  - [Zopieux] 引用了关于大量误报问题的文章，担心工具可能导致工程师花费大量时间处理不真实的漏洞。

• **工具的模型与技术基础**：
  - [czbvyRZNsVcpTm2] 询问开发者是否构建了自己的模型，以及目前表现最好的模型是什么。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提及工具的误报问题，以及对权限要求的担忧，反映了用户对工具可靠性和安全性的关注。
- 部分用户对工具的技术实现和与其他类似工具的区别表示好奇，希望获得更深入的技术解释。
- 对UI和用户体验的批评表明，用户对安全工具的易用性和透明度有较高要求。

data.title: Carbon Language: An experimental successor to C++
data.author: samuell
data.article_summary: Carbon Language是一项实验性项目，旨在成为C++的继承者，解决C++因技术债务和演进困难而面临的改进挑战。其目标包括与C++相匹配的性能、无缝双向互操作性、易于学习、高表达性以及可扩展的迁移。Carbon强调现代化和安全性，支持快速开发和现有C++代码的互操作与迁移。目前项目仍在开发中，团队正致力于构建编译器和工具链，并邀请开发者参与贡献。Carbon的独特之处在于其结合了多项关键目标，旨在继承并发展C++庞大的生态系统。项目尚未成熟，正在探索是否能获得足够的行业关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Carbon编程语言的定位、设计及其与C++和其他编程语言（如Rust、D、Zig）的关系。

不同观点：
• [kjksf] 认为Carbon的主要价值在于帮助大型C++项目（如Chrome）逐步迁移到更现代的语言，而不是一次性重写。Carbon允许在现有C++代码中混用，并提供工具自动转换代码，这是它与其他语言（如Rust、D、Zig等）最大的不同。
• [nxobject] 关注Carbon的长期发展路线图，指出其安全性的完整方案尚未确定，且开发进度较慢。此外，Carbon似乎主要在与C++社区讨论，而不是更广泛的编程语言社区，这可能限制其视角和创新。
• [Animats] 对Carbon在设计阶段未能解决安全性问题表示担忧，并指出已经有D和Zig等语言在这一领域存在，质疑Carbon的必要性。
• [NooneAtAll3] 认为Carbon不会流行，因为其语法（如"fn"和"var"）与C++差异较大，C++开发者可能因为代码外观不符合其编程习惯而不愿意采用。
• [JonChesterfield] 提出不一定需要Carbon来实现C++项目的转换，可以通过编译器将C++代码转换为Rust或D，并逐步调整代码风格。
• [verysorry42] 批评Carbon团队进展缓慢，质疑其能力与诚信，认为Google可能在浪费资源。
• [darksaints] 回忆Rust的早期语法讨论，认为Carbon的语法与当时被拒绝的Rust提案相似，如果Rust当时采用了该提案，可能会更受C++开发者欢迎。
• [benob] 质疑Carbon是否只是C++的语法糖，认为它可能只是为了控制语言演进，而不是提供C++无法实现的新功能。
• [Imustaskforhelp] 认为Zig是更好的选择，并对Carbon的推广方式（如通过某些YouTube频道）表示不满。
• [uvas_pasas_per] 建议将开发Carbon的精力用于构建Rust到C++的桥梁，可能更有价值。
• [z_open] 质疑是否所有主要编程语言都将由Web 2.0时代的企业控制。
• [ygritte] 询问不拥有稳定ABI的优点是什么。
• [imtringued] 认为Carbon的变化过多且不必要，给开发者增加了负担，但未能有效减轻C++的许多问题，类似于Python 3的迁移问题。
• [self_awareness] 对Carbon在类型指定时使用[]和()的不一致性表示困惑，但个人喜欢[]的用法，因为它类似于Scala。

补充讨论：
• Carbon语言的定位和设计目标引发了广泛争议，尤其是其与C++的兼容性、语法设计和开发进度。
• 安全性和ABI的稳定性是讨论的重要技术点。
• 一些评论者对Carbon的必要性表示怀疑，认为已有其他语言可以解决类似问题。
• 部分讨论涉及个人对语法和编程习惯的偏好，以及对语言演进方式的不满。

争议焦点：
• Carbon是否真正提供了独特的价值，特别是在已有Rust、D、Zig等语言的情况下。
• Carbon的开发进度和设计决策是否合理，尤其是其安全性和语法不一致的问题。

44745984.article_content:
Carbon Language:
An experimental successor to C++
Why?
|
Goals
|
Status
|
Getting started
|
Join us
See our
announcement video
from
CppNorth
.
Note that Carbon is
not ready for use
.
Fast and works with C++
Performance matching C++ using LLVM, with low-level access to bits and addresses
Interoperate with your existing C++ code, from inheritance to templates
Fast and scalable builds that work with your existing C++ build systems
Modern and evolving
Solid language foundations that are easy to learn, especially if you have used C++
Easy, tool-based upgrades between Carbon versions
Safer fundamentals, and an incremental path towards a memory-safe subset
Welcoming open-source community
Clear goals and priorities with robust governance
Community that works to be welcoming, inclusive, and friendly
Batteries-included approach: compiler, libraries, docs, tools, package manager, and more
Why build Carbon?
C++ remains the dominant programming language for performance-critical software, with massive and growing codebases and investments. However, it is struggling to improve and meet developers’ needs, as outlined above, in no small part due to accumulating decades of technical debt. Incrementally improving C++ is
extremely difficult
, both due to the technical debt itself and challenges with its evolution process. The best way to address these problems is to avoid inheriting the legacy of C or C++ directly, and instead start with solid language foundations like
modern generics system
, modular code organization, and consistent, simple syntax.
Existing modern languages already provide an excellent developer experience: Go, Swift, Kotlin, Rust, and many more.
Developers that
can
use one of these existing languages
should
.
Unfortunately, the designs of these languages present significant barriers to adoption and migration from C++. These barriers range from changes in the idiomatic design of software to performance overhead.
Carbon is fundamentally
a successor language approach
, rather than an attempt to incrementally evolve C++. It is designed around interoperability with C++ as well as large-scale adoption and migration for existing C++ codebases and developers. A successor language for C++ requires:
Performance matching C++
, an essential property for our developers.
Seamless, bidirectional interoperability with C++
, such that a library anywhere in an existing C++ stack can adopt Carbon without porting the rest.
A gentle learning curve
with reasonable familiarity for C++ developers.
Comparable expressivity
and support for existing software’s design and architecture.
Scalable migration
, with some level of source-to-source translation for idiomatic C++ code.
With this approach, we can build on top of C++’s existing ecosystem, and bring along existing investments, codebases, and developer populations. There are a few languages that have followed this model for other ecosystems, and Carbon aims to fill an analogous role for C++:
JavaScript → TypeScript
Java → Kotlin
C++ →
Carbon
Language Goals
We are designing Carbon to support:
Performance-critical software
Software and language evolution
Code that is easy to read, understand, and write
Practical safety and testing mechanisms
Fast and scalable development
Modern OS platforms, hardware architectures, and environments
Interoperability with and migration from existing C++ code
While many languages share subsets of these goals, what distinguishes Carbon is their combination.
We also have explicit
non-goals
for Carbon, notably including:
A stable
application binary interface
(ABI) for the entire language and library
Perfect backwards or forwards compatibility
Our detailed
goals
document fleshes out these ideas and provides a deeper view into our goals for the Carbon project and language.
Project status
Carbon Language is currently an experimental project. We are hard at work on a toolchain implementation with compiler and linker. You can try out the current state at
compiler-explorer.com
.
We want to better understand whether we can build a language that meets our successor language criteria, and whether the resulting language can gather a critical mass of interest within the larger C++ industry and community.
Currently, we have fleshed out several core aspects of both Carbon the project and the language:
The strategy of the Carbon Language and project.
An open-source project structure, governance model, and evolution process.
Critical and foundational aspects of the language design informed by our experience with C++ and the most difficult challenges we anticipate. This includes designs for:
Generics
Class types
Inheritance
Operator overloading
Lexical and syntactic structure
Code organization and modular structure
An under-development
compiler and toolchain
that will compile Carbon (and eventually C++ code as well) into standard executable code. This is where most of our current implementation efforts are directed.
Historically, there was also a prototype
explorer
interp

data.title: Our Farewell from Google Play
data.author: shakna
data.article_summary: SECUSO的"隐私友好应用"项目始于2016年，旨在提供仅需必要权限的替代应用，如手电筒应用。该项目在Google Play上提供了超过30个隐私友好应用，总安装量超过35万次。然而，由于在Google Play上维护应用更新的工作量过大，研究团队难以继续支撑。从2025年起，这些应用将不再通过Google Play提供更新，现有用户需转向F-Droid商店以获取持续支持和更新。现有安装不会受影响，但若不更新，可能因安卓系统变化而出现兼容性问题。SECUSO提供了迁移至F-Droid的指南，并感谢用户一直以来的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Play开发者政策对应用更新和维护的要求，及其对开发者和用户体验的影响

不同观点：
• **反对Google政策的观点**：
  - [a2128] 认为Google要求持续更新SDK的策略不合理，尤其是对那些自包含、离线使用、功能完整的应用而言。频繁的更新不仅耗费时间，还可能引入新bug，影响用户体验。
  - [ncruces] 提到自己的应用因无法持续更新而被下架，尽管这些应用以前有良好的盈利模式（如无干扰的广告），但现在被迫让位于充斥广告和追踪器的应用。
  - [dotdev] 也提到自己的十年老游戏因政策更新而被下架，无法快速重建，只能托管APK。
  - [suddenexample] 认为Google的政策让开发者难以发布高质量应用，希望Google能采取更开发者友好的政策，否则可能被其他平台取代。

• **支持或理解Google政策的观点**：
  - [hollowonepl] 认为Google的政策比Apple更宽松，尽管Google变得更加严格，但相对Apple而言仍更容易应对。
  - [liendolucas] 认为开发者应适应更新要求，否则会被淘汰，暗示行业变化不可避免。

• **替代方案的讨论**：
  - [muth02446] 提到将应用转换为PWAs（渐进式网络应用），解决了跨平台和减少维护负担的问题，但面临国际化（i18n）方面的挑战。
  - [_pdp_] 提到不依赖市场平台，而是直接与客户进行定制集成，从而避免繁琐的要求和收入损失。

• **其他相关案例**：
  - [rs186] 提到类似的情况发生在iOS游戏上，开发者因无法快速重建而受到影响。

补充讨论：
• **对Google政策的批评**：
  - [xorcist] 认为智能手机不断变化使得维护负担不合理，重新编译所有Windows软件每年看起来很荒谬，但在Android平台上却是常态。

Our Farewell from Google Play
Our project started in 2016 with the goal of offering alternatives to apps with basic functionality that demanded – back then at install time – many permissions they did not need. From our humble beginnings with Privacy Friendly Torchlight, our apps have always been available in the Google Play Store. Our current selection of Privacy Friendly Apps has grown since then to more than 30. And with more than 350,000 installs we believe we left a dent. We want to take this opportunity to also thank all our users for their continued support!
However, in 2025, eight years after we took on this project, things have changed. Not in regards to apps demanding more permissions than they need. No, unfortunately not that. What changed, however, is the effort to keep the apps updated. The maintenance for the provision of privacy-friendly apps in the Google Play Store is significantly greater than on F-Droid and is no longer feasible for a research group.
Please note that existing installations of our apps on your devices will not be deleted or affected by this change. However, you will no longer receive updates through the Google Play Store, which means that our apps may eventually stop working properly as the Android operating system evolves and compatibility issues arise. We recommend switching to the F-Droid Store for continued support and updates.
Our Privacy Friendly Apps will continue to be available on the F-Droid Store. For your convenience, we created instructions that explains how you can easily make the switch to the F-Droid Store while keeping all your data:

data.title: Show HN: An interactive dashboard to explore NYC rentals data
data.author: giulioco
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了纽约市（NYC）租赁市场的分析工具。用户可以通过选择不同的时间范围（如1个月、3个月、6个月、1年）查看租赁数据。工具提供多种筛选和自定义搜索选项，包括卧室数量（从工作室到4间以上）、浴室数量（从任意数量到4间以上），以及多种房源来源（如Leasebreak、Streeteasy、Craigslist等）。用户还可以通过点击地图选择具体社区，查看各区域的租赁市场洞察。该工具帮助用户根据个人需求精确定制和分析租赁市场数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纽约市租金变化、租房市场数据准确性及租房平台的功能与问题

不同观点：
• [rprend] 认为平台上的租金数据往往是房东的“期望价格”，而不是实际支付的价格。房东会通过各种手段使租金看起来比实际高，导致租金预期上升，进一步推动租金通胀。他以自己的租赁经验为例，指出合同上的租金远高于实际支付的租金，且租约中的优惠和押金机制存在误导。

• [cuuupid] 关注租金大幅上涨的现象，指出两年来2居室租金平均上涨超过25%。他讨论了租金上涨的原因，包括市场压力、房东的贪婪或市场泡沫，并提到即将上任的市长可能推动租金稳定政策，这可能对市场产生5%的衰退压力。

• [mbStavola] 指出租房平台在区域选择上存在错误，比如选择布鲁克林的Bay Ridge时，系统错误地包含了Staten Island的Westerleigh区域。

• [solumos] 对数据准确性提出质疑，指出DUMBO-Vinegar Hill—Downtown Brooklyn—Boerum Hill的租金中位数为2600美元，这看起来很可疑，且Crown Heights North区域没有数据。

• [jeffbee] 建议每个城市都应该有一个租赁登记系统，以避免从广告中猜测租金，提高租金数据的透明度和准确性。

• [asdev] 提出使用多模态AI过滤不符合居住标准的房源（如虚假的一居室、布局恶劣、无光照的公寓等），认为这样可以提高租金数据的准确性。

补充讨论：
• [adi_hn07] 对平台的用户界面和功能提出了具体的技术反馈，如API访问、网页抓取及注册流程中的bug。

• [kevin11111] 和 [suncemoje] 对平台的设计表示赞赏，但未深入讨论具体内容。

• [cyberax] 提到纽约市需要增加住房密度以降低成本，暗示增加住房供应可能是解决高租金问题的一个途径。

• [msukkarieh] 和 [AvAn12] 对纽约市某些区域的高租金表示惊讶和怀疑，侧面反映了对数据真实性的关注。

争议焦点：
• 租房市场数据的不透明和不准确性，尤其是房东虚抬租金价格和平台数据错误的问题。
• 租金上涨的原因，是市场压力、房东贪婪还是市场泡沫，以及租金稳定政策可能带来的影响。

data.title: Online Safety Act: What went wrong?
data.author: olyellybelly
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国网络内容管控措施及其可行性、技术实现和政府角色

不同观点：
• Zak认为，虽然不应让儿童观看色情内容，但当前这一问题并不严重，不需采取有较大负面影响的严格解决方案。他支持通过浏览器设置和家长控制来减少儿童偶然接触色情内容，而不必进行过度干预。
• Alexisread指出，政府无视撤销管控的请愿，暗示政府倾向于支持审查制度，而不是倾听公众意见。
• Havoc对政府在网络问题上的应对能力缺乏信心，认为政府会继续采用无效的管控方法，如增加监管和惩罚，而不是寻找技术解决方案。
• Holowoodman反对将整个互联网变为“儿童安全”环境，认为应该通过教育和家长监督来解决问题，而不是依赖政府控制和技术手段。
• VikingMiner提到，一些议员提出不切实际的建议（如出售没有尖端的菜刀）来解决社会问题，显示出对技术现实的误解。
• K1t建议政府应要求网站提供“儿童安全模式”，并通过DNS解析来实现，这样可以简化家长控制，同时避免过于技术化的操作。
• Randallsquared批评作者认为法律不够专制以实现其目标，暗示法律的严厉程度并非解决问题的关键。
• Arp242指出，虽然现有的家长控制工具能够阻止儿童访问有害内容，但这些工具的使用体验较差，需要技术社区开发更易用的标准和工具。
• Ok123456关注政府在身份验证系统上的准备不足和第三方验证网站的信任问题，同时批评政府以“保护儿童”为借口扩大监管范围。
• TheBigSalad认为政策的真正测试应该是其预期结果，而不是实施和执行过程。
• _joel批评政府和工党在网络管控问题上的处理方式，导致公众不满。
• Azalemeth分享了一份请愿链接，显示出大量公众反对当前的管控措施。
• Exasperated提出一个值得探讨的问题，即某些大型内容平台在不同国家法律下的选择性合规行为，暗示背后有政治和商业考量。
• Amoe_认为用刀具犯罪的类比不恰当，因为英国已经有购买刀具的年龄限制，显示出对不同类型管控措施的双重标准。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效保护儿童免受有害网络内容的影响，是通过技术手段（如浏览器设置、家长控制）还是通过政府政策和法律监管。
• 对政府在管控措施中的角色和能力存在广泛不信任，许多人认为政府缺乏技术理解，且管控措施可能带来负面后果。
• 技术社区被指出在开发易用的家长控制工具和标准方面还有很大改进空间。
• 公众对政府请愿的反应显示出对现有管控措施的强烈反对。

data.title: GPT-5 is already (ostensibly) available via API
data.author: consumer451
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT-5短暂通过API提供但现已下架的事件，及其相关影响和背景

不同观点：
• [ameliaquining] 建议将标题更改为 "GPT-5 was briefly (ostensibly) available via API"（GPT-5曾短暂通过API提供），因为目前该模型已下架。该评论强调了GPT-5的暂时性和目前不可用状态。

data.title: Long Term Support
data.author: rishikeshs
data.article_summary: SQLite旨在提供小巧、快速、可靠的数据库解决方案，计划持续支持到2050年。它具有跨平台特性，能够在多种操作系统和硬件上运行，且数据库文件在不同系统间无需转换。SQLite的文件格式稳定且文档详尽，有助于未来几十年的可读写性。代码经过严格的航空级测试，确保稳健性，并通过详尽的注释和文档帮助新开发者快速上手。此外，SQLite的源代码历史和备份分布在全球多个数据中心，以应对灾难。开发团队注重长期可维护性，并承诺保持C语言API和磁盘格式的向后兼容性，确保现有应用程序能够在未来版本中继续使用。美国国会图书馆也推荐将SQLite作为数字内容保存的存储格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SQLite的未来发展、技术特点及其维护模式

不同观点：
• **SQLite未来发展的可持续性**：
  - [arp242] 担心SQLite主要开发者Richard Hipp年纪渐长，未来可能不再参与开发，但认为由于SQLite是开源项目，其未来依然有保障，类似于Rust和Go语言在赞助停止后的情况。
  - [aanthonymax] 认为SQLite已经有25年历史，开发者对未来有长远计划，表现出了可持续性。

• **SQLite的维护和文档质量**：
  - [stego-tech] 强调SQLite源代码中超过35%是注释，认为高质量的文档降低了新维护者进入的门槛，有助于项目的长期维护。
  - [tmaly] 以自身经历为例，表示自己2008年编写的SQLite代码至今仍能正常运行，证明其维护成本低。

• **SQLite的技术特点和应用场景**：
  - [wiz21c] 对SQLite的“航空级测试”表示赞赏，但质疑这种高标准测试的成本和需求方。
  - [pikuseru] 希望更多软件能像SQLite一样进行开发和支持。
  - [haunter] 认为SQLite虽然能应对局部灾难，但无法应对全球性灾难，除非有人将其移植到Collapse OS或Dusk OS上。

补充讨论：
• **关于编程趋势和风格的讨论**：
  - [breadwinner] 赞赏SQLite开发者避免追逐编程潮流，提到其他开发者为了显得不落伍而过度使用C#新特性。
  - [declan_roberts] 进一步指出SQLite的开发理念是编写不受时间影响、易于维护的代码，隐含对追逐潮流的Rust社区的批评。

• **其他技术细节和趣闻**：
  - [kej] 提到可以通过“a/an”的使用来判断一个人的口音，是一个与技术无关但有趣的语言现象。

• **SQLite高标准测试的必要性和成本**：[wiz21c] 对SQLite的高标准测试（如航空级测试）表示赞赏，但对其成本和谁为此买单提出疑问。这涉及项目的实际需求与资源投入之间的平衡问题。

Long Term Support
The intent of the developers is to support SQLite through
the year 2050.
At this writing, 2050 is still 25 years in the future.
Nobody knows what will happen in that time, and we cannot
absolutely promise that SQLite will be viable or useful that
far out.
But we can promise this: we plan as if we will be
supporting SQLite until 2050.
That long-term outlook affects our
decisions in important ways.
Cross-platform Code
→
SQLite runs on any platform with an 8-bit byte,
two's complement 32-bit and 64-bit integers,
and a C compiler.  It is actively
tested on all currently popular CPUs and operating
systems.
The extreme portability of the SQLite code and file
format will help it remain viable on future platforms.
Stable, Cross-platform Database Files
→
SQLite
database files
are bit-for-bit identical on
32-bit, 64-bit, big-endian, and little-endian platforms.  You
can copy an SQLite database file from one system to another
without having to translate or convert the database.
Furthermore, the file format is well documented and stable.
Database files created today will be readable and writable by
future versions of SQLite decades in the future.
Aviation-grade testing
→
Every machine-code branch instruction is tested in both
directions.  Multiple times.  On multiple platforms and with
multiple compilers.  This helps make the code robust for
future migrations.  The intense testing also means that new
developers can make experimental enhancements to SQLite and,
assuming legacy tests all pass, be reasonably sure that the
enhancement does not break legacy.
Extensive, detailed documentation
→
SQLite has candid, developer-friendly,
and open-source documentation.  Docs are written by and
for programmers.
(A few examples:
[1]
[2]
[3]
[4]
[5]
[6]
[7]
[8]
)
The extensive documentation helps new developers
come up to speed on SQLite very quickly.
Heavily commented source code
→
The SQLite source code is over 35% comment.  Not boiler-plate
comments, but useful comments that explain the meaning of variables
and objects and the intent of methods and procedures.
The code is designed
to be accessible to new programmers and maintainable over a span
of decades.
Disaster planning
→
Every byte of source-code history for SQLite is cryptographically
protected and is automatically replicated to multiple
geographically separated servers, in datacenters
owned by different companies.
Thousands of additional clones exist on private servers around the
world.
The primary developers of SQLite live in different regions of the world.
SQLite can survive a continental catastrophe.
Old school
→
Nobody is completely immune to trends and fads, but the SQLite
developers work hard to avoid being sucked into the latest programming
fashion.  Our aim is to produce timeless code that will be
readable, understandable, and maintainable by programmers
who have not yet been born.
In addition to "supporting" SQLite through the year 2050, the developers
also promise to keep the SQLite
C-language API
and
on-disk format
fully backwards compatible.
This means that application written to use SQLite today should be able to
link against and use future versions of SQLite released decades in the
future.
Our goal is to make the content you store in SQLite today as
easily accessible to your grandchildren as it is to you.
Update on 2018-05-31:
Our goal of supporting SQLite long-term have apparently come to the
notice of the preservationist at the
US Library Of Congress
who have identified
SQLite as a
recommended storage format
for the preservation of
digital content.

data.author: p-sharpe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI personas和多代理模拟平台的应用及其潜在问题，特别是在市场营销、产品反馈和政策咨询中的使用。

不同观点：
• **对AI personas伦理和可持续性的担忧**：[milchek] 认为使用AI personas模拟焦点小组虽然能提高反馈规模、降低成本，但忽略了真实反馈的本质。AI无法体验社区生活，仅是训练数据的反映，可能导致基于合成信号的决策失误。特别是在地方政府咨询中的使用令人担忧。
• **技术实现与长期模拟稳定性**：[arkokoley] 分享了其在多代理模拟框架（SALM）上的研究，提出通过层次化提示架构和注意力记忆系统，实现长期模拟稳定性，并认为其研究可以为提升AI personas的准确性和可预测性提供帮助。
• **产品定位与市场适应性**：[chatmasta] 强调需要明确目标买家和核心功能，避免产品功能泛化。讨论了数据收集和现有客户数据整合的重要性，并建议与数据经纪公司合作以增强数据丰富性。
• **实际数据的多样性与模型表现**：[digitcatphd] 指出LLM的结果在多样性和真实世界数据补充方面仍有不足，认为目前的AI personas还不能完全替代真实世界的反馈。
• **对模型准确性的质疑**：[rollinDyno] 对模型准确性评估标准提出疑问，并希望看到与其他行业标准模型的比较结果。
• **对实际调研价值的怀疑**：[StarterPro] 认为依赖AI模拟反馈可能违背实际调研的目的，认为只有基于真实买家的输入才有意义。

补充讨论：
• **目标买家与使用场景**：[chatmasta] 提出需要明确目标买家，例如产品发现和内容营销，并讨论了产品与现有客户数据的整合方式。
• **技术实现细节**：[lucasverra] 和 [bodhi_mind] 对平台在LinkedIn和其他社交媒体上的应用表现出兴趣，并询问了技术实现细节，如网站测试和本地开发网站的支持。
• **潜在合作与市场反馈**：[impostervt] 和 [pwillia7] 对使用AI personas增强产品设计表示兴趣，并认为平台的推出非常有价值。

整体来看，讨论围绕AI personas的应用潜力与技术、伦理挑战展开，涵盖了市场定位、技术实现、数据质量和模型准确性等多个方面。争议焦点主要集中在AI personas能否替代真实人类反馈及其在地方政府决策中的应用伦理问题。

data.title: How did Facebook intercept competitor's encrypted mobile app traffic? (2024)
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: Meta正面临一项集体诉讼，指控其可能违反了《窃听法》。根据法院文件和对Onavo Protect应用的逆向工程分析，Meta被指通过中间人（MITM）攻击拦截用户的加密HTTPS流量，该技术被称为“ssl bump”，用于解密特定Snapchat、YouTube和Amazon域名的流量。Onavo Protect Android应用要求用户安装由“Facebook Research”颁发的证书，以解密TLS流量。尽管该应用有超过1000万次安装，但新版Android系统的安全控制使得该方法不再有效。目前尚不清楚所有用户流量是否都被拦截。此案实际上是一起反垄断诉讼，指控Meta违反了《谢尔曼法》，而关于《窃听法》的指控是附带发现的。此外，Facebook还考虑滥用Android的辅助功能API获取敏感数据，这种行为通常与恶意软件相关联。Meta的动机是为了获取竞争对手如Snapchat的可靠分析数据。

44755528.article_content:
There is a current class action lawsuit against Meta in which court documents note* that the the company may have breached the
Wiretap Act
. The analysis made in this post is based on content
court documents
and reverse engineering sections of archived Onavo Protect app packages for Android.
It is said that Facebook intercepted user's encrypted HTTPS traffic by using what would be considered the a
MITM attack
. Facebook called this technique "ssl bump", appropriately named after the transparent proxy
feature
in the
Squid caching
proxy software which was used to (allegedly) decrypt specific Snapchat, YouTube and Amazon domain(s).  It is suggested to read a recent
TechCrunch
article for additional background on the case.
[2024-07-28] - Note this is different to what TechCrunch
had revealed in 2019
in which Facebook were paying teenagers to gather data on usage habits. That resulted in the Onavo app being pulled from the app stores and
fines
. With the new MITM information revealed: what is currently unclear is if all app users had their traffic "intercepted" or just a subset of users.
*
A HN user
clarifies
:
"This is not a wiretapping case. It's an antitrust case; the claims are all for violations of the Sherman Act. Plaintiffs' attorneys _incidentally_ found evidence during discovery that Facebook may have breached the Wiretap Act."
Case 3:20-cv-08570-JD Document 735 Filed 03/23/24 Page 1
Due to the limited and partial information, some facts may be inaccurate or incomplete in this post. As such this post is subject to updates if corrections are warranted or new discoveries made. Feel free to
subscribe
to this blog to receive new content to your inbox, or follow me on
X
.
Technical Summary
Onavo Protect Android app
, which had over
10 million
Android installations, contained code to prompt the user to install a CA (certificate authority) certificate issued by "Facebook Research" in the user trust store of the device. This certificate was required for Facebook to decrypt TLS traffic.
Some versions of the older app contain the Facebook Research CA certs as embedded assets in the distributed app from 2016. One cert is valid until 2027. Data discovery content in court documents state certificates are "generated on the server and sent to the device".
Soon after the "ssl bump" feature was deployed in the Protect app, a newer version of Android was released that included improved security controls that would render this method unusable on devices with the newer operating system.
A review of an old Snapchat app shows that it's analytics domain did not employ certificate pinning, meaning that MITM / "ssl bumping" would have worked as described.
In addition to the core functionality of gathering other app's usage statistics through abusing a permission granted by the user, there also appears to be other functionality to obtain questionable sensitive data, such as the
subscriber IMSI
.
The setup most likely would have looked something the following diagram:
An interpretation of FB's setup based on court documents and app analysis
Here we have a trusted cert installed on the device, all device traffic going over a VPN to Facebook controlled infrastructure, traffic redirected into a Squid caching proxy setup as a transparent proxy with the 'ssl bump' feature configured. We know from the documents that various domains belonging to Snapchat, Amazon and Youtube were of interest. It's not known if any other user traffic was intercepted, or just proxied on. This type of information we can't obtain from looking at the archived Onavo Protect apps, rather for the time being, we have to rely on the content in the court documents made available to the public.
Over time the success of their strategy to employ a transparent TLS proxy was diminishing due to improved security controls in Android.  Additionally certificate pinning adoption was said to be an issue. As an alterative, Facebook were considering using the
Accessibility API
as an alternative.
Page 3 - Case 3:20-cv-08570-JD Document 736
This is what Google has to say about using the accessibility features on their operating system:
"only services that are designed to help people with disabilities access their device or otherwise overcome challenges stemming from their disabilities are eligible to declare that they are accessibility tools."
It's somewhat telling of a company that would consider abusing features designed to support people with disabilities for a competitive advantage. Generally, Android accessibility functionality misuse is attributed to malicious applications such as
banking malware
.
Motivation
Mark Zuckerberg states the need for "
reliable analytics
" on Snapchat:
The solution? "
Kits that can be installed on iOS and Android that intercept traffic for specific sub-domains
":
My take on the above is that in addition to utilizing the Onavo Protect VPN app to intercept traffic for specific domains, there was an intention to rebrand the core technology and havin
44755528.article_summary: Meta正面临一项集体诉讼，指控其可能违反了《窃听法》。根据法院文件和对Onavo Protect应用的逆向工程分析，Meta被指通过中间人（MITM）攻击拦截用户的加密HTTPS流量，该技术被称为“ssl bump”，用于解密特定Snapchat、YouTube和Amazon域名的流量。Onavo Protect Android应用要求用户安装由“Facebook Research”颁发的证书，以解密TLS流量。尽管该应用有超过1000万次安装，但新版Android系统的安全控制使得该方法不再有效。目前尚不清楚所有用户流量是否都被拦截。此案实际上是一起反垄断诉讼，指控Meta违反了《谢尔曼法》，而关于《窃听法》的指控是附带发现的。此外，Facebook还考虑滥用Android的辅助功能API获取敏感数据，这种行为通常与恶意软件相关联。Meta的动机是为了获取竞争对手如Snapchat的可靠分析数据。

data.article_summary: Onshape是领先的云原生CAD和PDM平台，支持任何设备运行，不会崩溃或丢失数据，并通过分支和合并简化协作。它提供实时协作、自动保存和无限版本恢复，适合设计专业人士和教育机构使用。新用户可免费试用Onshape Professional长达6个月，无需信用卡。Onshape还具备内置的PDM、版本控制和安全管理功能，已被众多SOLIDWORKS用户和设计领导者采用。平台提供丰富的学习资源和现代化的CAD工具，助力团队提升设计效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Onshape这款CAD软件的功能、许可问题及其替代方案

不同观点：
• [malfist] 指出，Onshape的免费个人许可要求用户在平台上制作的任何内容的所有权都归Onshape，用户需要注意这一点，特别是如果他们打算出售自己的设计。
• [WillAdams] 提供了开源替代方案的概述，包括BRL CAD、FreeCAD、Solvespace和Dune 3D，并提到OpenSCAD和Python相关的设计工具。他还指出Onshape免费账户的文档是公开的。

• [barrystaes] 分享了他使用Onshape设计功能性3D打印部件的经验，强调其跨设备使用的便利性和参数化设计的优势。

data.title: Belgium bans Internet Archive's ‘Open Library’
data.author: gslin
data.article_summary: 比利时布鲁塞尔商业法院发布了一项广泛的封锁令，目标包括互联网档案馆的“开放图书馆”项目以及其他盗版网站，如Anna’s Archive、LibGen和Z-Library。这些网站被指控未经授权提供书籍下载，构成侵权。该命令要求比利时的互联网服务提供商（ISP）、域名解析服务、搜索引擎、支付中介等多个 intermediaries 封锁相关网站，包括谷歌、微软、Cloudflare、亚马逊网络服务等公司。互联网档案馆未被听取意见即被下达封锁令，显示出命令的单方面性。此次封锁是比利时打击盗版措施的一部分，但引发了对网络自由和合法性的广泛讨论。此前，互联网档案馆在美国因类似诉讼败诉，导致部分书籍下架。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：比利时及欧洲可能的审查和信息控制措施，以及其对信息自由和隐私的影响。

不同观点：
• **paulyy_y**：认为欧洲将出现严苛的监督和审查制度，并可能被极端势力滥用。如果中央实体控制信息访问，信息的完整性和持久性将无法得到保障，类似情况在美国也在发生。
• **xeiotos**：质疑民主制度的有效性，认为政府日益变得复杂且成本高昂，主要由大公司和富豪操控，普通公民难以影响决策，同时自己承担高额税负。
• **conartist6**：反对个别小国法官通过全球性禁令，认为这会导致全球规则的退步，并对此表示强烈反对。
• **amelius**：对比利时科技领域发生的事件感到惊讶，尝试寻找相关新闻未果，表明对事件缺乏了解。
• **the_biot**：认为文章对审查的新颖性过于惊讶，指出比利时ISP多年来一直在封锁盗版网站，且市场由少数公司主导。
• **kmfrk**：提到Open Library等免费平台可能在比利时不再可能存在，对这种信息限制表示不满。
• **visarga**：讨论了出版商限制书籍使用的方式，如禁止扫描、在线借阅、训练LLM等，认为这限制了思想自由重用，是个人的净损失。
• **anonzzzies**：呼吁开发p2p、去中心化、强加密的应用框架，以应对可能的政府审查和封锁。

• **buyucu**：推荐使用Mullvad VPN来应对信息封锁。
• **MaxPock**：预测欧洲将很快禁止书籍。
• **piokoch**：提到西欧不仅购买俄罗斯石油和天然气，还可能借鉴某些政治理念，对此表示不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于信息自由与版权保护之间的平衡，以及政府和中央实体在控制信息访问中的角色。
• 对民主制度有效性的质疑，以及大公司和富豪对政府决策的影响也被提出。
• 有人担心个别国家的司法裁决可能对全球产生影响，并对此表示反对。
• 技术解决方案如VPN和去中心化框架被认为是应对审查的可能手段。

44755441.article_content:
Belgium Bans Internet Archive’s ‘Open Library’ in Sweeping Site Blocking Order
Traditional site-blocking measures that require local ISPs to block subscriber access to popular pirate sites are in common use around the world.
The aim is to deter piracy by making sites more difficult to find, but these measures are only partially effective.
More recently, site-blocking requests have begun to target other intermediaries. This includes DNS providers, such as Google and Cloudflare, which were ordered to block sites in France, Italy, and elsewhere.
A few months ago DNS blocking arrived in Belgium, where several orders required both ISPs and DNS resolvers to restrict access to pirate sites. This prompted significant pushback, most notably Cisco’s OpenDNS ceasing operations in the country.
Broad Blocking Order Targets Internet Archive’s ‘Open Library’
A new order, issued by the Brussels Business Court in mid-July, targets an even broader set of intermediaries and stands out for other reasons as well.
Requested by various publishing and author organizations, the order aims to block access to known pirate libraries including Anna’s Archive, LibGen, OceanofPDF, and Z-Library. In addition, it also targets the Internet Archive’s
Open Library
project.
Target Sites (in Dutch)
Open Library was created by the late
Aaron Swartz
and Internet Archive’s founder Brewster Kahle, among others. As an open library its goal is to archive all published books, allowing patrons to borrow copies of them online.
The library aims to operate similarly to other libraries, loaning only one copy per book at a time. Instead of licensing digital copies, however, it has an in-house scanning operation to create and archive its own copies.
Open Library
The Open Library project was previously sued by publishers in the United States, where the Internet Archive ultimately
losing
the case. As a result, over 500,000 books were made unavailable.
However, many other books remain available to patrons. The authors and publishers in Belgium argue that, since this is done without permission, the site should be blocked alongside Anna’s Archive, LibGen and Z-Library.
Clear and Significant Infringement
The rightsholders describe Open Library as a website where registered members of the public can easily access and download their books. This includes 1,542 works from the publisher Dupuis, over 5,000 works from the publisher Casterman, and many others.
According to the publishers, the operators of the Open Library are not easily identified, while legally required information is allegedly missing from the site, which they see as an indication that the site is meant to operate illegally.
This description seems at odds with the fact that Open Library is part of the Internet Archive, which is a U.S.-registered  501(c)(3) non-profit.
From the order (in Dutch)
The publishers also reference a U.S. court order in favor of other publishers, which allegedly confirms the unlawful nature of Open Library.
The Brussels court, after reviewing these arguments and the submitted evidence, concluded that there was a
prima facie
case of “clear and significant infringement,” which justified granting a provisional blocking order against Open Library and the other targeted sites.
Broad Blocking Order Targets ISPs, Search, Payments, and More
Internet Archive was not heard in this case, as the blocking order was issued
ex parte
, without its knowledge. This is remarkable, as the organization is a legal entity in the United States, which receives support from many American libraries.
The broad nature of the order doesn’t stop there either. In addition to requiring ISPs, including Elon Musk’s Starlink, to block the library’s domain names, it also directs a broad range of other intermediaries to take action.
This includes search engines, DNS resolvers, advertisers, domain name services, CDNs, and hosting companies. An abbreviated overview of the requested measures is as follows;
—
Search Engines
Google
must remove the target sites from search results, deactivate related Google Ads, remove an infringing app from the Google Play Store, and block DNS requests for the associated domains.
Microsoft
is ordered to remove the target sites from the “Bing” search engine and block related DNS queries.
Hosting, DNS, CDNs, and Domain Name Services
The following companies must terminate hosting, and deactivate or suspend the domain names of the target sites: Hostinger, GoDaddy, Amazon Web Services, SEDO, Cloudflare, Unmanaged Ltd, AlexHost, and Internet Archive.
Payment Intermediaries
These companies are ordered to suspend all payment services benefiting the target sites: Alipay (Europe), Cash App and Squareup Europe, and PayPal (Europe).
ISPs including Starlink
The following ISPs, active in Belgium, are required to implement DNS blocking measures: Telenet, Proximus, Mobile Vikings, Orange Belgium, Voo, DIGI Communications, Cybernet, EDPnet, CENTREA, Yoin, Tchamba Refinder, IPTelecom, United Mobile, SkyDS

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于信息自由与版权保护之间的平衡，以及政府和中央实体在控制信息访问中的角色。
• 对民主制度有效性的质疑，以及大公司和富豪对政府决策的影响也被提出。

data.title: Google shifts goo.gl policy: Inactive links deactivated, active links preserved
data.author: shuuji3
data.article_summary: Google此前宣布将于2025年8月25日停止支持所有goo.gl短链接，但现调整了计划，决定保留仍在使用的链接。对于2024年底无活动的链接，Google已重定向并提示将在8月失效，只有这些不活跃链接会被停用。若看到“此链接即将失效”的消息，建议更换其他短链接服务。其他goo.gl链接将继续正常工作，用户可访问链接检查是否保留。如果链接直接重定向且无提示，则将继续有效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google 停止支持其短链接服务（goo.gl）的决定及其影响

不同观点：
• Jasonpeacock 认为，删除用户数据的决定令人惊讶，特别是考虑到这些链接广泛嵌入在各种文档、视频和帖子中。他质疑产品经理是如何考虑用户使用场景的。
• Neilv 指出，这个决定可能违背了“不作恶”的原则。他认为，即使不再接受新链接，Google 也有责任保留现有的链接数据，并保持其可访问性。
• Shuuji3 提供了一种解决方案，通过运行ArchiveTeam Warrior来帮助将链接存档到Internet Archive，以应对链接失效的问题。
• Modeless 质疑“停用”链接的目的，认为此举没有明确的意义。
• Nsksl 和 Dang 对链接被停用的标准感到困惑，尤其是当链接仍然收到点击时被认为是“不活跃”的。
• Xp84 推测，Google 可能因为品牌安全问题（如钓鱼攻击）而停止了该服务，并建议使用无明显品牌标识的短链接服务。
• Uehreka 用讽刺的语气强调“酷URL永不改变”，表达了对Google此举的不满，并提到可能转向其他短链接服务如bit.ly。
• Quink 用比喻的方式批评Google，认为其行为像是在随意撕毁未读的书页，暗示对用户的不尊重。
• Alpb 和 Mixdup 认为，维持这项服务的成本很低，Google 可以选择继续提供这项服务或将数据存档到公共平台如Archive.org。
• Jjice 和 Yandie 则认为，Google 此举可能是为了节省成本，但相对于其负面影响，这样的成本节省并不值得。

补充讨论：
• ChrisArchitect 提到Google现在使用https://share.google替代goo.gl，并询问是否与.gl TLD有关。
• BeanjuiceII 表达了对Google整体信任的丧失，质疑其在其他服务上的可靠性。

争议焦点：
• Google 停用goo.gl服务的合理性以及其对用户数据处理的责任问题。
• 停用标准的不明确性以及对链接仍被使用但被停用的困惑。
• 服务成本与用户体验之间的平衡，以及Google品牌安全与用户信任的取舍。

44759918.article_content:
While we
previously announced
discontinuing support for all goo.gl URLs after August 25, 2025, we've adjusted our approach in order to preserve actively used links.
We understand these links are embedded in countless documents, videos, posts and more, and we appreciate the input received.
Nine months ago, we redirected URLs that showed no activity in late 2024 to a message specifying that the link would be deactivated in August, and these are the only links targeted to be deactivated. If you get a message that states, “This link will no longer work in the near future”, the link won't work after August 25 and we recommend transitioning to another URL shortener if you haven’t already.
All other goo.gl links will be preserved and will continue to function as normal. To check if your link will be retained, visit the link today. If your link redirects you without a message, it will continue to work.

data.title: Supporting the BEAM community with free CI/CD security audits
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Erlang Solutions为BEAM社区提供支持，包括为开源Erlang和Elixir项目提供免费的CI/CD安全审计，帮助发现和修复漏洞。这些审计通过SAFE工具实现，集成于开发管道中，如GitHub Actions、CircleCI和Jenkins，自动扫描代码以提前发现问题。审计结果在几分钟内生成，反馈清晰且具可操作性。开源维护者可通过邮件申请免费许可，时长根据项目需求确定。此外，Erlang Solutions还提供专家主导的生产系统审计服务，涵盖代码审查、架构评估和性能审计等。公司通过赞助会议、支持基金会和社区项目等方式，全面支持BEAM生态系统的发展。更多信息可在社区中心获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Erlang的BEAM虚拟机及其相关话题的讨论，包括技术定义、开源许可争议、以及其他技术社区中的现象和网站显示问题。

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为 BEAM 是 Erlang 的运行时解释器（虚拟机），并指出该术语不广为人知，因为在 Acronym Finder 中找不到相关解释，尽管在 Wikipedia 上有定义。
• [mananaysiempre] 关注的是 Erlang 提供的 SAFE 开源许可证问题。他们指出，该许可证的条款限制了像 Curl 这样的完全开源项目的商业支持，认为条款不够清晰且存在潜在矛盾。他们引用了具体条款，特别是禁止任何商业使用的规定，认为这可能不符合一些开源维护者的需求。
• [citizenpaul] 提出了一个观察，询问最近几个月是否有一些与 Erlang 相关的趋势或活动，因为他们频繁看到 BEAM 被提及，自己可能错过了某些技术圈内的动态。
• [victorbjorklund] 则关注的是网站的用户体验问题，提到网站在其浏览器上的字体看起来被拉伸，存在显示问题。

补充讨论：
• [lagniappe] 认为关于文章标题的讨论不应带有主观色彩，指出标题已经清楚表达了内容，无需过度解读或修改。
• 争议的焦点在于 [mananaysiempre] 对 Erlang 的 SAFE 许可证条款的质疑，尤其是这些条款是否真正符合开源社区的需求。他们以 Curl 项目为例，指出这种限制性条款可能对一些开源维护者不适用。

总结：讨论主要围绕 Erlang 的 BEAM 虚拟机、开源许可证 SAFE 的适用性、技术社区的趋势以及网站显示问题。开源许可证的条款是否合理是争议的核心，而其他讨论点则涉及技术术语的认知、技术趋势的关注以及网站的用户体验问题。

44758957.article_content:
Sign up for our quarterly newsletter
Keep up to date with the latest news, best practice ideas and exclusive offers. Don’t miss out. Sign up here.
At Erlang Solutions, our support for the BEAM community is long-standing and built into everything we do. From contributing to open-source tools and sponsoring events to improving security and shaping ecosystem standards, we’re proud to play an active role in helping the BEAM ecosystem grow and thrive.
One way we’re putting that support into action is by offering free CI/CD-based security audits for open-source Erlang and Elixir projects. These audits help maintainers identify and fix vulnerabilities early, integrated directly into modern development workflows.
What the Free CI/CD Audits Offer
Our free CI/CD security audits for open source projects are powered by
SAFE (Security Audit for Erlang/Elixir)
, a dedicated solution built to detect vulnerabilities in Erlang and Elixir code that could leave systems exposed to cyber attacks.
The CI/CD version of SAFE integrates directly into your development pipeline (e.g. GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Jenkins), enabling you to scan for vulnerabilities automatically every time code is committed or updated. This helps projects:
Detect issues early, before they reach production
Maintain a more secure and resilient codebase
Improve visibility of risks within day-to-day workflows
Results are delivered quickly– typically within a few minutes. For larger codebases, it may take up to 20–30 minutes. The feedback is designed to be clear, actionable, and minimally disruptive.
Open source maintainers can request a free license by emailing safe@erlang-solutions.com and including a link to their repository. Once approved, we provide a SAFE license for one month or up to a year, depending on the project’s needs, at no cost.
For more information, read our
full terms and conditions
.
Expert-Led Audits for Production BEAM Systems
SAFE is just one way we help teams build secure, resilient systems. We also offer hands-on audit services for production systems, including:
Code reviews
focused on clarity, maintainability, and best practices
Architecture assessments
to help ensure systems are scalable and fault-tolerant
Performance audits
to identify bottlenecks and optimise how systems behave under load
These services are delivered by our in-house experts and are a great fit for teams working on complex or business-critical systems. They also pair well with SAFE for a full picture of how systems are running and how they could be even better.
Of course, supporting the BEAM community goes beyond security and audits. Our involvement spans education, events, and long-term ecosystem development.
“We’re proud to support the BEAM ecosystem not just with code, but with the infrastructure and insights that help it grow stronger,” says Zoltan Literati, Business Unit Leader at Erlang Solutions Hungary.
“Our free audits offer real, practical value to maintainers working in open source. It’s one of the ways we’re giving back to the community.”
A Broader Commitment to the BEAM Community
The BEAM ecosystem continues to grow across languages like Erlang, Elixir and Gleam, driven by a global community of developers, maintainers, educators and advocates. Erlang Solutions is proud to contribute across multiple fronts, including:
Sponsoring various conferences, including
Code Sync
Supporting the
Erlang Ecosystem Foundation (EEF)
, including participation in working groups focused on security, documentation, interoperability, and tooling
Backing inclusion-focused initiatives such as
Women in BEAM
Sharing learning resources, contributing to open source libraries, and facilitating knowledge exchange through meetups, blogs and webinars
Our role is to support the ecosystem not only through expertise, but through action, and to help ensure that BEAM-based systems are not only scalable and reliable, but secure.
To learn more about our free CI/CD security audits or how we support the BEAM community, visit
our community hub
.
Erlang Solutions Team
Our content team comprises a diverse array of contributors hailing from various corners of Erlang Solutions. With a keen eye for emerging trends and a passion for our capabilities, we delve into the forefront of industry developments, we strive to deliver content that captivates and informs.

data.title: Hyrum's Law
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: Hyrum's Law指出，当一个API拥有足够多的用户时，不论其约定如何，系统的所有可观察行为都会被某些用户依赖。这是由于用户会无意中依赖接口暴露或隐藏的实现细节，形成所谓的“隐式接口”。这种现象逐渐限制了系统实现的修改自由，因为这些修改不仅要符合显式接口，还要满足用户对隐式接口的预期，导致“bug-for-bug compatibility”的情况。随着系统扩展，隐式接口最终会完全映射到实现上，使实现成为新的接口，限制系统的演化。因此，设计和维护复杂系统时需考虑隐式接口的影响。Hyrum's Law由Hyrum Wright提出，得名于他的观察和Titus Winters的推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hyrum's Law在软件工程中的影响以及如何处理用户对未明确保证的行为的依赖

不同观点：
• **用户依赖未明确保证的行为是不可避免的**：avidiax指出，即使合同中明确否认某种行为的保证，用户仍会依赖该行为。例如，队列系统即使只能保证"最多一次"或"至少一次"的传递，但如果实际通常提供"恰好一次"，用户会依赖这一行为。数据桶服务即使不保证性能，但如果通常提供100MB/s的吞吐量，用户会期望这一性能。

• **Hyrum's Law对API设计者的挑战**：AdamH12113认为，从API设计者的角度来看，Hyrum's Law必须被考虑，但从用户的角度来看，依赖未明确保证的行为是工程上的不当行为。用户应理解并承担依赖实现细节的风险，并且在实现细节改变时没有合理的理由抱怨。

• **"末日论者解释"与"公开与私有接口"的区分**：kibwen提出"末日论者解释Hyrum's Law"，认为实现细节的改变必须符合公开文档化的接口以及隐含的使用接口。同时，强调将接口细节分类为"公开"和"私有"是为了在用户依赖私有行为时有道德高地可以拒绝他们的要求。

• **历史与技术背景的例子**：atakan_gurkan提到Commodore 64中的非法操作码，认为这些操作码之所以保留是因为用户依赖它们。cafard则引用《The Mythical Man-Month》中提到的用户依赖未明确但实际一致的行为。

• **LLM和AI生成代码的影响**：prats226讨论了LLM（大型语言模型）世界中Hyrum's Law的影响，指出LLM的输出没有明确的合同保证，只有可观察的行为，且行为可能随每次更新而改变，下游系统需要评估来应对这种变化。

• **随机化实现以 discourage 依赖**：nvader建议通过随机化实现细节来防止用户依赖内部行为，例如Go语言中地图遍历顺序的随机化。

• **API中的断言选项**：amelius建议API应具有"assertions"选项，以确保API调用也能进行断言/不变量检查。

补充讨论：
• **XKCD漫画的引用**：TehCorwiz引用XKCD漫画来幽默地反映Hyrum's Law的影响。

• **软件作者的规则定义权**：kiitos强调软件作者有权定义软件的规则，认为Hyrum's Law描述了一种常见问题，但并不定义预期的规则或要求。如果用户依赖未明确保证的行为，责任在于用户自身。

争议焦点：
• **用户依赖未明确保证的行为的责任归属**：一方认为软件作者应考虑用户对未明确保证行为的依赖，另一方认为用户应自行承担依赖这些行为的风险，责任在于用户。

44757755.article_content:
Hyrum's Law
An observation on Software Engineering
Put succinctly, the observation is this:
With a sufficient number of users of an API,
it does not matter what you promise in the contract:
all observable behaviors of your system
will be depended on by somebody.
Over the past couple years of doing low-level infrastructure migrations in one of the most complex software systems on the planet, Iâve made some observations about the differences between an interface and its implementations.  We typically think of the interface as an abstraction for interacting with a system (like the steering wheel and pedals in a car), and the implementation as the way the system does its work (wheels and an engine).  This is useful for a number of reasons, foremost among them that most useful systems rapidly become too complex for a single individual or group to completely understand, and abstractions are essential to managing that complexity.
Defining the correct level of abstraction is a completely separate discussion (see Mythical Man-Month), but we like to think that once an abstraction is defined, it is concrete.  In other words, an interface should theoretically provide a clear separation between consumers of a system and its implementers.  In practice, this theory breaks down as the use of a system grows and its users start to rely upon implementation details intentionally exposed through the interface, or which they divine through regular use.  Spolskyâs âLaw of Leaky Abstractionsâ embodies consumersâ reliance upon internal implementation details.
Taken to its logical extreme, this leads to the following observation, colloquially referred to as âThe Law of Implicit Interfacesâ: Given enough use, there is no such thing as a private implementation.  That is, if an interface has enough consumers, they will collectively depend on every aspect of the implementation, intentionally or not.  This effect serves to constrain changes to the implementation, which must now conform to both the explicitly documented interface, as well as the implicit interface captured by usage.  We often refer to this phenomenon as "bug-for-bug compatibility."
The creation of the implicit interface usually happens gradually, and interface consumers generally arenât aware as itâs happening.  For example, an interface may make no guarantees about performance, yet consumers often come to expect a certain level of performance from its implementation.  Those expectations become part of the implicit interface to a system, and changes to the system must maintain these performance characteristics to continue functioning for its consumers.
Not all consumers depend upon the same implicit interface, but given enough consumers, the implicit interface will eventually exactly match the implementation.  At this point, the interface has evaporated: the implementation has become the interface, and any changes to it will violate consumer expectations.  With a bit of luck, widespread, comprehensive, and automated testing can detect these new expectations but not ameliorate them.
Implicit interfaces result from the organic growth of large systems, and while we may wish the problem did not exist, designers and engineers would be wise to consider it when building and maintaining complex systems.  So be aware of how the implicit interface constrains your system design and evolution, and know that for any reasonably popular system, the interface reaches much deeper than you think.
Who's Hyrum?
I'm a Principal Scientist at Adobe, and before that, a software engineer at Google.  I work on large-scale code change tooling and infrastructure, and spent several years improving Google's core C++ libraries.  The above observation grew out of experiences when even the simplest library change caused failures in some far off system.
While I may have made the observation, credit goes to Titus Winters for actually naming it as "Hyrum's Law" and popularizing the concept more broadly.

44757755.article_summary: Hyrum's Law指出，当一个API拥有足够多的用户时，不论其约定如何，系统的所有可观察行为都会被某些用户依赖。这是由于用户会无意中依赖接口暴露或隐藏的实现细节，形成所谓的“隐式接口”。这种现象逐渐限制了系统实现的修改自由，因为这些修改不仅要符合显式接口，还要满足用户对隐式接口的预期，导致“bug-for-bug compatibility”的情况。随着系统扩展，隐式接口最终会完全映射到实现上，使实现成为新的接口，限制系统的演化。因此，设计和维护复杂系统时需考虑隐式接口的影响。Hyrum's Law由Hyrum Wright提出，得名于他的观察和Titus Winters的推广。

data.article_summary: 17岁的汉娜·开罗（Hannah Cairo）解决了一个长达40年的数学猜想，令数学界震惊。她自小在巴哈马接受家庭教育，通过在线课程和自学完成了高等数学课程，11岁就学完了微积分。她对数学的深入探索使她感到家庭教育的局限性，因此她申请参加了伯克利的一个研究生课程。在那里，她构造出一个行为异常的函数，推翻了米佐哈塔-竹内猜想（Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture），这一成果挑战了数学家对函数行为的常规认知。尽管她的学习路径非传统，但她的数学天赋和成就获得了广泛认可。开罗谦逊且不认为自己特别出色，但她无疑已成为数学界的一颗新星。

At 17, Hannah Cairo Solved a Major Math Mystery
By
Kevin Hartnett
August 1, 2025
After finding the homeschooling life confining, the teen petitioned her way into a graduate class at Berkeley, where she ended up disproving a 40-year-old conjecture.
Comment
Save Article
Read Later
Valerie Plesch for
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Kevin Hartnett
Contributing Writer
August 1, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
geometry
mathematics
All topics
It’s not that anyone ever said sophisticated math problems can’t be solved by teenagers who haven’t finished high school. But the odds of such a result would have seemed long.
Yet
a paper posted on February 10
left the math world by turns stunned, delighted and ready to welcome a bold new talent into its midst. Its author was
Hannah Cairo
, just 17 at the time. She had solved a 40-year-old mystery about how functions behave, called the Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture.
“We were all shocked, absolutely. I don’t remember ever seeing anything like that,” said
Itamar Oliveira
of the University of Birmingham, who has spent the past two years trying to prove that the conjecture was true. In her paper, Cairo showed that it’s false. The result defies mathematicians’ usual intuitions about what functions can and cannot do.
So does Cairo herself, who found her way to a proof after years of homeschooling in isolation and an unorthodox path through the math world.
A World Without Bounds
Cairo grew up in Nassau, the Bahamas, where her parents had moved so that her dad could take a job as a software developer. She and her two brothers — one three years older, the other eight years younger — were all homeschooled. Cairo started learning math using Khan Academy’s online lessons, and she quickly advanced through its standard curriculum. By the time she was 11 years old, she’d finished calculus.
Soon she had consumed everything that was readily available online. Her parents found a couple of math professors to tutor her remotely — first Martin Magid of Wellesley College, then Amir Aazami from Clark University. But much of her education was self-directed, as she read and absorbed, on her own, the graduate-level math textbooks that her tutors recommended. “Eventually,” Cairo recalled, Aazami “said something like, he feels uncomfortable being paid, because he feels like he’s not really teaching me. Because mostly I would read the book and try to prove the theorems.”

Hannah Cairo taught herself the equivalent of an advanced undergraduate math curriculum by the time she was 14.
Valerie Plesch for
Quanta Magazine
But Cairo found homeschooling confining.
“There was this inescapable sameness, in a way. No matter what I did, I was in the same place doing mostly the same things,” she said. “I was very isolated, and nothing I could do could really change that. I’d wake up on certain days and realize, I’m just older.”
Math became a kind of escape, a space that felt expansive when her daily life was not.
“Mathematics was another world I could explore. A world that was not confining, a world I could access at any point just by thinking about it,” she said. “That’s how I grew up, thinking about mathematics as this world of ideas that I can explore on my own. That sort of process helped me see math differently than a lot of people.”
In 2021, amid the Covid pandemic, Cairo’s world began to widen, even as it was narrowing for so many others. Travel restrictions stranded her family at her grandparents’ house in Chicago. While they were there, she joined the Math Circles of Chicago, where teachers and students gather to solve difficult problems together.
The experience led her to apply the following year to a two-week online summer program run by the Berkeley Math Circle, which has nurtured some of the most exceptional math talent in the world. In her application, she listed a set of self-taught subjects that together comprised the equivalent of an advanced undergraduate math degree. She was 14 years old.
As a teenager, Cairo constructed a function that behaved in strange and unexpected ways, disproving a major conjecture in a field called Fourier restriction theory.
Valerie Plesch for
Quanta Magazine
“Hannah is above and beyond the ordinary,” said
Zvezdelina Stankova
, a mathematician at Berkeley and the founder of the Berkeley Math Circle. “Every time she applies for school or a program, she is several levels ahead.”
Yet these scattered experiences never convinced Cairo that she had exceptional mathematical ability. She is soft-spoken, open and humble, and seems genuinely unsure of how her ability stacks up against anyone else’s — in part because for y

data.article_summary:
文章列举了多个快速完成 ambitious 项目的例子：

1. **BankAmericard**：Dee Hock 在90天内从零开始推出，吸引超过10万客户。
2. **P-80 Shooting Star**：Kelly Johnson 的团队在143天内设计并交付了美国空军首架喷气战斗机。
3. **Marinship**：在收到 telegram 后的197天内建成船厂并完成首艘船。
4. **The Spirit of St. Louis**：Donald Hall 和 Charles Lindbergh 在60天内设计并制造了这架飞机。
5. **Eiffel Tower**：用793天建成，成为当时世界最高建筑。
6. **Treasure Island**：用约两年时间在旧金山湾建造了人工岛。
7. **Apollo 8**：NASA 在134天内决定并实现了登月任务。
8. **The Alaska Highway**：用234天建成1,700英里的军用公路。
9. **Disneyland**：在366天内建成。
10. **The Empire State Building**：用410天建成。
11. **The Berlin Airlift**：在463天内完成大规模空运任务，并建成 Tegel 机场。
12. **The Pentagon**：用491天建成，设计和建造极为迅速。
13. **Boeing 747**：用约930天完成从决定到首架飞机的制造。
14. **The New York Subway**：首条线路用时4.7年，后续扩展项目耗时更长。

这些例子展示了高效团队在短时间内完成复杂项目的能力。

Source:

.
Marinship.
"Shipyard construction was begun promptly after a telegram from the United States Maritime Commission was received by the W. A. Bechtel Company. The telegram was received on 2 March 1942, the Sausalito site selected on 3 March, and a proposal to build the shipyard presented in Washington DC was made on 9 March. Ten minutes into the presentation U. S. Maritime Commission administrators told the W.A. Bechtel Company to build the shipyard. Physical construction began on 28 March. Construction start was delayed two weeks to allow the 42 families living on Pine Point, which was scheduled to be demolished to build the shipyard, to move." The first ship was completed on September 15 of that year, 197 days after receiving the telegram.
Source:
Marinship on the Fast Track
.
The Spirit of St. Louis.
In 1927, Donald Hall and Charles Lindbergh designed and built
Spirit
in 60 days. The Eiffel Tower was built in 2 years and 2 months; that is, in 793 days. When completed in 1889, it became the tallest building in the world, a record it held for more than 40 years. It cost about $40 million in 2019 dollars.

In 1935, San Francisco decided to commemorate the completion of the Golden Gate and Bay Bridges by building a new island as a home for the Golden Gate International Exposition. On August 9 1968, NASA decided that Apollo 8 should go to the moon. It launched on December 21 1968, 134 days later.

On average, a supply aircraft landed every 2 minutes for 14 months. As part of this effort, Tegel airport was built. 3. **Marinship**：在收到 telegram 后的197天内建成船厂并完成首艘船。
4. **The Spirit of St. Louis**：Donald Hall 和 Charles Lindbergh 在60天内设计并制造了这架飞机。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过被雇佣来解决个人遇到的软件问题，以及软件质量和用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• [b8] 分享了自己因被亚马逊误判欺诈而封禁，通过内部联系反欺诈团队迅速解封的经历。这表明有时通过内部渠道解决问题比联系客服更有效。
• [stevesimmons] 提到Google Maps无法记住用户的距离单位偏好，讽刺其用户 profiling 的核心目标未实现，暗示软件功能不够人性化。
• [11Spades] 对文章的排版提出建议，认为页面边缘留白可以提升阅读体验，属于对文章排版的反馈。
• [SoftTalker] 强调应用不应在用户输入完成前执行操作，例如搜索时自动执行，建议等待用户停止输入后再执行操作。
• [zac23or] 认为当前软件质量低下，解决问题可能比自己被雇佣去修复更困难，引用了GTA 5加载时间问题的例子。

补充讨论：
• [stavros] 指出文章未提及雇佣过程，而这其实是整个事件的核心部分，认为文章内容不够完整。
• [hinkley] 分享了自己在知识产权律师严格管控下的工作经历，说明即使不能直接提交代码，通过精确描述问题也能帮助解决问题。
• [Sytten] 指出AbortController只能停止客户端请求，无法阻止服务器端继续处理，批评一些搜索功能在用户离开后仍在后台运行。
• [PantaloonFlames] 简短评论了取消操作的显而易见性。
• [buggy6257] 提到自己曾试图进入Discord修复自动巨大表情的问题，显示用户为改善体验愿意采取极端措施。
• [cosmic_quanta] 提到George Hotz在Twitter短暂工作以修复登录弹窗的例子，暗示某些技术牛人解决问题后迅速离开，具有讽刺意味。
• [syntaxing] 回忆了苹果公司的一个传说，某员工抱怨多年未解决的macOS问题，入职后解决并辞职，暗示公司内部问题需内部解决。
• [sitzkrieg] 讽刺那些对苹果公司持积极态度的人，指出他们被诱导列出各种问题。
• [khazhoux] 提出短期加入不同软件团队以修复自己关心的特定功能的想法，例如加入Logic Pro团队改进乐谱工具，或修复iOS音乐应用的特定问题。

争议焦点：
• 软件质量与用户体验问题是否只能通过内部雇佣解决，外部用户反馈是否有效。
• 应用自动执行操作（如搜索、过滤）是否合理，是否应等待用户明确指示。
• 用户对大公司软件功能不满意，是否有更好的渠道或方法促使问题解决。

总结：评论主要围绕通过雇佣解决个人软件问题、软件质量不高以及用户体验不佳展开讨论，涉及具体案例和个人经历，并讨论了可能的解决方案和改进建议。

data.title: Pseudo, a Common Lisp macro for pseudocode expressions
data.author: reikonomusha
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种将大型语言模型（LLM）嵌入Common Lisp编程语言的构思，通过`pseudo`宏将自然语言描述自动转换为S表达式。该宏利用LLM将伪代码扩展为实际代码，并结合上下文信息（如可见变量、函数符号、源代码等）生成符合要求的代码。虽然此方法在Lisp中可行，但存在LLM的常见问题，如速度慢、成本高、结果不可预测或错误。目前，`pseudo`依赖于Google的Gemini作为后端，并需要一些外部库支持。作者提醒不要在生产环境中使用此功能，并提供了代码下载和依赖库信息以供实验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过LLM（大型语言模型）和大括号语言（如Lisp和JavaScript）进行Prompt工程和代码生成的可行性与潜在问题

不同观点：
• **soegaard**：引用了William Bowman的演讲，对使用LLM进行Prompt工程持批评态度，暗示这种方法可能不是一个好主意，并通过RacketCon的例子来说明不同LLM的性能差异。

• **tluyben2**：对使用Lisp展示LLM能力表示赞赏，认为Lisp比JavaScript的实现更为优雅。同时指出某些LLM（如openai/gpt-4o-mini）能更好地完成任务，而其他一些则表现不佳。

• **xigoi**：以讽刺的口吻指出，经过数十年的研究，我们现在可以让程序在每次编译时以不可预测的方式崩溃，暗示这种方法可能带来不稳定性。

• **cryptonector**：以幽默的语气指出，不能将伪代码直接投入生产环境，因为可能会导致不一致的结果，强调了代码可靠性的重要性。

• **JonChesterfield**：认为传递词法信息并要求返回S表达式是一个好主意，建议增加缓存机制以记住LLM上次的结果，从而形成一种合法但略显奇怪的语言实现。

• **jlarocco**：认为这种方法很有趣，并提出了一种宏的设想，可以通过搜索GitHub上的函数实现来增强可预测性。

补充讨论：
• **nurettin**：提到了在相关内容中看到大量18+广告，虽然与技术讨论无关，但指出了内容管理方面的问题。

争议焦点：
• 使用LLM进行代码生成的可靠性和可预测性是主要的争议点。不同评论者对LLM在代码生成中的表现持有不同的看法，有的批评其不稳定性，有的则认为在特定情况下表现尚可。

• 代码实现的可生产性也是讨论的重点，部分评论者质疑将LLM生成的伪代码直接用于生产环境的可行性。

44726641.article_content:
I was wondering what it would look like if a large language model
were part of your programming language.  I'm not talking about
calling the model as an API, but rather embedding it as a language
construct.  I came up with this idea as a first cut.
The
pseudo
macro allows you to embed pseudocode
expressions in your Common Lisp code.  It takes a string description
and uses an LLM to expand it into an s-expression.  You can
use
pseudo
anywhere an expression would be
expected.
(defun my-func (a b)
(pseudo "multiply b by factorial of a."))
MY-FUNC
(my-func 5 3)
360
(defun quadratic (a b c)
(let ((d (sqrt (pseudo "compute discriminant of quadratic equation"))))
(values (/ (+ (- b) d) (* 2 a)) (/ (- (- b) d) (* 2 a)))))
QUADRATIC
(quadratic 1 2 -3)
1.0
-3.0
The
pseudo
macro gathers contextual information and
packages it up in a big set of system instructions to the LLM.  The
instructions include
the lexically visible variables in the macro
environment
fbound symbols
bound symbols
overall directives to influence code generation
directives to influence the style of the generated code
(functional vs. imperative)
directives to influence the use of the loop macro (prefer
vs. avoid)
the source code of the file currently being compiled, if there
is one
pseduo
sets the LLM to use a low temperature for more
predictable generation.  It prints the “thinking” of the
LLM.
Lisp is a big win here.  Since Lisp's macro system operates at the
level of s-expressions, it has more contextual information available
to it than a macro system that is just text expansion.  The
s-expression representation means that we don't need to interface
with the language's parser or compiler to operate on the syntax tree
of the code.  Adding
pseudo
to a language like Java
would be a much more significant undertaking.
pseudo
has the usual LLM caveats:
The LLM is slow.
The LLM can be expensive.
The LLM can produce unpredictable and unwanted code.
The LLM can produce incorrect code; the more precise you
are in your pseudocode, the more likely you are to get the results
you want.
You would be absolutely mad to use this in production.
pseudo
has one dependency on SBCL which is a function
to extract the lexically visible variables from the macro
environment.  If you port it to another Common Lisp, you'll want to
provide an equivalent function.
pseudo
was developed using Google's Gemini as the back
end, but there's no reason it couldn't be adapted to use other
LLMs.  To try it out, you'll need the gemini library, available
at
https://github.com/jrm-code-project/gemini
,
and a Google API key.
Download
pseudo
from
https://github.com/jrm-code-project/pseudo
.
You'll also need these dependencies.
alexandria
— available from Quicklisp
cl-json
— available from Quicklisp
dexador
— available from Quicklisp
fold
—
https://github.com/jrm-code-project/fold
function
—
https://github.com/jrm-code-project/function
named-let
—
https://github.com/jrm-code-project/named-let
uiop
— available from Quicklisp
If you try it, let me know how it goes.

• **jlarocco**：认为这种方法很有趣，并提出了一种宏的设想，可以通过搜索GitHub上的函数实现来增强可预测性。

补充讨论：
• **nurettin**：提到了在相关内容中看到大量18+广告，虽然与技术讨论无关，但指出了内容管理方面的问题。

争议焦点：
• 使用LLM进行代码生成的可靠性和可预测性是主要的争议点。不同评论者对LLM在代码生成中的表现持有不同的看法，有的批评其不稳定性，有的则认为在特定情况下表现尚可。

• 代码实现的可生产性也是讨论的重点，部分评论者质疑将LLM生成的伪代码直接用于生产环境的可行性。

data.title: Make Your Own Backup System – Part 2: Forging the FreeBSD Backup Stronghold
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论备份服务器的配置和策略。作者偏好使用FreeBSD作为备份服务器的操作系统，并根据需要选择专业备份服务或完全控制备份磁盘。对于IPv4和IPv6，作者采用不同的网络配置方法，并强调使用VPN和防火墙增强安全性。作者建议将备份服务分割到不同的jail或虚拟机中，并使用ZFS文件系统增加灵活性。他强调本地和远程备份的结合，以确保数据安全，并建议备份服务器应具备磁盘冗余和加密。备份服务器应尽量与外部网络隔离，并通过VPN访问，以增强安全性，防止数据泄露或被盗。作者还提醒，备份必须存放在与生产数据不同的数据中心，以防灾难性事件导致数据丢失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何通过权限管理增强备份安全性，避免攻击者破坏生产环境后进一步删除备份。

不同观点：
• Benlivengood 认为使用 `zfs allow` 命令可以有效授予非根用户仅向其数据集添加快照的权限，从而防止攻击者删除备份。这种方法虽然需要手动清理旧快照，但能显著降低风险。
• 他还提到可以通过分工进一步增强安全性，例如让发送快照的朋友无法以 root 身份登录备份服务器，从而限制其权限，避免潜在的破坏行为。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了 `zfs allow` 命令的具体应用场景，即通过限制用户权限来防止攻击者在攻陷生产环境后进一步删除备份数据，这是一种纵深防御策略。
• 强调了手动清理旧快照的额外工作量，但认为这种风险降低是值得的，表明在安全性和操作复杂性之间做出了权衡。
• 提到了权限分工的策略，通过限制 root 登录权限，进一步缩小了潜在攻击面，这是一种最小权限原则的应用。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于手动清理旧快照的操作复杂性和额外工作量是否值得，这涉及到对安全性和操作效率的不同优先级权衡。有些人可能认为自动化清理更为理想，而另一些人则可能更看重手动操作带来的安全性提升。

44720285.article_content:
Laying the Foundation
With the
primary backup strategies and methodologies introduced
, we've reached the point where we can get specific: the Backup Server configuration.
When choosing the type of backup server to use, I tend to favor specific setups: either I trust a professional backup service provider (like Colin Percival's
Tarsnap
), or I want full control over the disks where the backups will be hosted. In both cases, for the past twenty years, my operating system of choice for backup servers has been FreeBSD. With a few rare exceptions for clients with special requests, it covers all my needs. When I require Linux-based solutions, such as the
Proxmox Backup Server
, I create a VM and manage it within.
I typically use both IPv4 and IPv6. For IPv4, I "play" with NAT and port forwarding. For IPv6, I tend to assign a public IPv6 address to each jail or VM, which is then filtered by the physical server's firewall. Unfortunately, every provider, server, and setup has a different approach to IPv6, making it impossible to cover them all in this article. When a provider allows for routed setups, I use this approach:
Make your own VPN: FreeBSD, WireGuard, IPv6, and ad-blocking included
- assigning a /72 to the bridge for the jails and VMs.
In my opinion, FreeBSD is a perfect all-rounder for backups, thanks to its ability to completely partition services. You can separate backup services (or specific servers/clients) into different jails or even VMs. Furthermore, using ZFS greatly enhances both flexibility and the range of tools you can use.
The main distinction is usually between local backup servers (physically accessible, though not always attended, and in locations deemed secure) and remote ones, such as leased external servers. I personally use a combination of both. If the services I need to back up are external, in a datacenter, and need to be quickly restorable, I prefer to always have a copy on another server in a different datacenter with good outbound connectivity. This guarantees good bandwidth for restores, which isn't always available from a local connection to the outside world. However, an internal, nearby, and accessible backup server (even a Raspberry Pi or a mini PC) ensures physical access to the data. Whenever possible, I maintain both an external and an internal copy - and they are autonomous, meaning the internal copy is
not
a replica of the external one, but an additional, independent backup. This ensures that if a problem occurs with the external backup, it won't automatically propagate to the internal one. In any case, the backup must always be in a different datacenter from the one containing the production data. When
the fire at the OVH datacenter in Strasbourg
caused the entire complex to shut down, many people found themselves in trouble because their backups were in the same, now unreachable, location. I had a copy with another provider, in a different datacenter and country, as well as a local copy.
Despite it being "just" a backup server, I almost always use some form of disk redundancy. If I have two disks, I set up a mirror. With three or more, I use RaidZ1 or RaidZ2. This is because, in my view, backups are nearly as important as production data. The inability to recover data from a backup means it's lost forever. And it happens often, very often, that someone contacts me to recover a file (or a database, etc.) days or weeks after its accidental loss or deletion. Usually, pulling out a file from a two-month-old backup generates a mix of disbelief, admiration, but above all, a sense of security in the person requesting it. And that is what our work should instill in the people we collaborate with.
The backup server should be hardened. If possible, it should be protected and unreachable from the outside. My best backup servers are those accessible only via VPN, capable of pulling the data on their own. If they are on a LAN, it's even better if they are completely disconnected from the Internet.
For this very reason,
backups must always be encrypted
. Having a backup means having full access to the data, and the backup server is the prime target for being breached or stolen if the goal is to get your hands on that data. I've seen healthcare facilities' backup servers being targeted (in a rather trivial way, to be honest) by journalists looking for health details of important figures. It is therefore critical that the backup server be as secure as possible.
Based on the type of access, I use two types of encryption:
If the server is local
(especially if the ZFS pool is on external disks), I usually install FreeBSD on UFS in read-only mode, as
I've described in a previous article
, and encrypt the backup disks with
GELI
. This ensures that in the event of a "dirty" shutdown (more likely in unattended environments), I can reconnect to the host and then reactivate the ZFS pool. This approach makes it nearly impossible to retrieve even the pool's metadata if the disks are stolen, as

data.title: Show HN: Pontoon – Open-source customer data syncs
data.author: alexdriedger
data.article_summary: Pontoon是一个开源、自托管的数据导出平台，专为将数据产品交付给企业客户而设计。它支持将数据直接同步到客户的数据仓库（如Snowflake、BigQuery、Redshift），无需客户构建ETL工具，从而节省时间和成本。Pontoon提供易于部署、自动化同步、多云支持、可扩展架构和Web界面管理等功能，还支持REST API进行编程访问。与传统API相比，Pontoon解决了性能问题、客户体验差和速率限制等挑战。与其他ETL平台不同，Pontoon主要供供应商用作产品功能提供给客户的数据团队，且完全开源，支持自托管。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pontoon平台的许可问题、技术功能以及与类似平台的区别。

不同观点：
• ConorMcCarter（Prequel联合创始人）对Pontoon发布的祝贺，并提到Prequel实际上支持自托管，同时讨论了市场前景以及欧盟数据法案对软件供应商的潜在影响。他还提供了技术建议，指出Snowflake正在淘汰单因素用户名/密码认证，建议Pontoon尽快支持密钥对认证以减少用户迁移成本。

• Mdaniel对Pontoon的许可证问题提出了强烈批评，认为其在开源声明上存在误导性。他指出顶级许可证文件包含两个许可证，并且使用了一种复杂的许可结构（包含类似if语句的条件），最终默认使用非开源的Elastic License 2.0。他还表达了对这种不透明许可方式的反感，认为这是在试图欺骗开发者贡献代码。

补充讨论：
• Hiatus对比较表中“First-class Data Products”一行表示疑惑，希望得到进一步解释，这表明技术功能细节上存在信息不明确的地方。

• A2128指出了Pontoon与Mozilla的Pontoon翻译平台的区别，避免混淆，提供了一个相关链接以帮助用户区分两者。

• Melson对Pontoon的功能进行了简单询问，提出了是否类似于“离线同步”的功能，表明用户对平台具体功能实现方式存在疑问。

争议焦点：
• Pontoon的许可证问题成为讨论中的争议焦点，mdaniel强烈反对其当前的许可证结构，认为其不透明且具有误导性。
• 技术实现上的细节（如认证方式、数据产品功能、离线同步等）也存在一些疑问和需要澄清的地方。

About
Pontoon is an open source, self-hosted, data export platform. We built Pontoon from the ground up for the use case of shipping data products to your enterprise customers.
Pontoon is engineered to make it easy to sync data directly to your customer's data warehouse (eg.
Snowflake
,
BigQuery
, and
Redshift
). Your customers get their data, without needing to build ETLs or pay for ETL tools, empowering them to make data driven decisions for their business, with data from your product.
Welcome to the future of customer data syncs 🚀
Want to get Pontoon up and running in minutes? Try our
Quick Start Guide
.
Key Features
🚀 Easy Deployment
:
Get started
in minutes with Docker or deploy to
AWS Fargate
🎯 Major Data Warehouses Integrations
: Supports
Snowflake
,
Google BigQuery
,
Amazon Redshift
, and
Postgres
as sources and destinations
☁️ Multi-cloud
: Send data from any cloud to any cloud. Amazon Redshift ➡️ Google BigQuery? No problem!
⚡ Automated Syncs
: Schedule data transfers with automatic backfills. Incremental loads automatically keep destination datasets in sync
🏗️ Built for Scale
: Sync over 1 million records per minute
✨ Web Interface
: User-friendly dashboard for managing syncs, built with React/Nextjs
🔌 REST API
: Programmatic access to all Pontoon features, built with FastAPI
✅ Open Source
: Complete control over your data and infrastructure with zero lock-in
The Problem with APIs & Data
Data Export with APIs
We built Pontoon because traditional APIs are becoming increasingly problematic at modern data scale:
Performance Issues
: APIs struggle with large datasets and complex queries
Poor Customer Experience
: Customers have to spend weeks building ETLs or pay for managed ETL tools ($$$)
Rate Limits
: Data workloads tend to be bursty, often triggering rate limits, resulting in a frustrating experience for everyone involved
Backfills
: Backfilling historical data through APIs is inherently slow, as most APIs are optimized for real-time, not bulk ingestion
Data Export with Pontoon
Pontoon solves these problems with:
Direct Warehouse Integration
: Send data directly to customer's data warehouse. No more ETLs needed!
Scalable Architecture
: Handle millions of rows efficiently. Say goodbye to rate limits!
Automated Scheduled Syncs
: Automatically keep destinations up to date, only syncing data that's changed/new. Backfills are completed on the first sync.
Self-Hosted
: Full control over your data and infrastructure
Is Pontoon Just Another ETL Platform?
Short Answer:
No.
ETL platforms are used by data teams to
pull data out
of vendors (eg. Salesforce). Data teams maintain/pay for the ETL platform.
Pontoon is used by vendors (eg. Salesforce) to
provide data syncs
as a product feature for their customer's data team. The vendor deploys Pontoon.

data.title: Ergonomic keyboarding with the Svalboard: a half-year retrospective
data.author: Twey
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己作为计算机用户和键盘爱好者的经历，特别是为了缓解重复性劳损（RSI）而转向使用Dvorak键盘布局，并逐渐探索各种人体工学键盘的历程。作者详细介绍了使用过的几款键盘，如Microsoft Ergonomic系列和Kinesis Advantage，但最钟爱的还是Ergodox EZ。他强调了分体式设计、帐篷式摆放和拇指集群等功能对减轻手腕和肘部疼痛的重要性。此外，作者对键盘的可编程性有高度需求，因其独特的输入习惯和速记爱好。最后，作者提到对CharaChorder的尝试，尽管其紧凑设计和和弦输入有潜力提升打字速度，但因其操作系统封闭和配置限制而未能完全实现作者的期望。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人体工学键盘的设计、使用体验及其潜在的健康影响

不同观点：

My background
Â§
E
ven before I started pressing buttons for a living I was always a
pretty heavy computer user.  When I was about 18 I started
experiencing symptoms of RSI.  At around the same time I learnt of the
Dvorak keyboard layout, and so I switched, hoping it would solve my
problems.  It did, at least at the time, and so for the last 17 years
Iâve been a Dvorak user.
A
t the same time Iâm really interested in human/machine interaction
and ways to get the contents of the human brain into a machine as
fluently as possible.  As a combined result of these two factors, I
worked my way through a few different physical keyboards, including
the Microsoft Ergonomic series (which I struggled to make Windows 2000
recognize â go figure) and a Kinesis Advantage, but my keyboard of
choice for many years now has been the
Ergodox EZ
.  The Ergodox (and its ZSA
comrade the Moonlander) is a solid keyboard, with a few features that
Iâve come to realize are very important:
Split halves
. Any keyboard with the halves joined together (that is
narrower than shoulder-width, as is the case with every joined
keyboard Iâve seen so far) causes the elbows to bend in and the wrists
to bend out, which seems to be the primary trigger of wrist pain
for me.
Tenting
. Ditto for the elbows: last year I found myself struggling
with pain and numbness in my arm that, on investigation, matched
symptoms of early cubital tunnel syndrome.  Tenting, rotating the
halves of the keyboard so that the wrists sit in a slight angle,
allows the elbows to rest in a more natural slightly-bent position,
and since adopting it I havenât had any further problems with my elbow.
Figure 1. The Microsoft Ergonomic Keyboard.
Thumb clusters
. The first symptom I got was whatâs affectionately
known as âemacs pinkyâ.
In fact, on most keyboards (though sadly no longer on ThinkPads) the control key, positioned in the bottom-right corner, can and should be held with the palm â this makes some combinations more awkward, though no more awkward than with the little finger, and saves the weakest digit.  In fact, I think it would be better named for vi â the escape key is perhaps the least ergonomic key on a standard keyboard.  Some people like to put it in the place of caps-lock, which is of course entirely missing the point.
The
reason I picked up the Kinesis Advantage is that on these keyboards
the thumb, which is highly underutilized in standard layouts, gets a
dedicated cluster of keys, perfect for things like modifiers, since
the opposable thumbs donât limit the motion of the rest of the hand at
all, no matter how itâs engaged.
Figure 2. The Kinesis Advantage.  This one is wireless, while mine, the original model, was connected by PS/2 cable.  But the layout hasnât changed.
Programmability
. My customization is light compared to some
peopleâs, but my keyboard usage is pretty idiosyncratic, so itâs
important to me to be able to customize my keyboard when I need to.
Particularly for keyboards with fewer keys that need heavier layer
usage, I want to be able to set up the layers as I want.  My most
elaborate customization is that I am (from time to time) a hobbyist
stenographer
, and rather
than having a separate device I find it convenient to be able to
configure my keyboard to speak one of the steno protocols understood
by
Plover
such as TX
Bolt or GeminiPR.
Finger-oriented keyboarding
Â§
W
ith this in mind, I was pretty excited when I stumbled across the
CharaChorder
.  The promise is
simple: increase typing speed through a combination of minimizing
finger movement and stenography-style chording (albeit with a theory
designed to have a shallower learning curve, basically just mashing
all the letters of the word at once).  I signed up to the
pre-order, and when I got it I immediately started playing around,
practising a few hours per day on the (very good!) training software.
Figure 3. The CharaChorder One.
I
f youâve ever done typing training, youâll know that most of the
point of the drills and forms that they teach you is to keep your
fingers on the home row so that you can reach all the letters with a
minimum of movement.  The CharaChorder turns this on its head: on the
CharaChorder there is
only
the home row.  Where you would stretch up
or down or sideways to reach a key on a traditional keyboard, on the
CharaChorder you simply wiggle a joystick in that direction, never
taking your finger off the key.
There is in fact a second row of joysticks used for arrow keys or mouse emulation, but weâll ignore them for the purposes of this since they donât impact most of the typing experience.
I
loved the compact form factor combined with the power of chording,
and I was excited to develop a new steno theory based on the
CharaChorderâs unique structure.  Unfortunately, I was thwarted: the
CC1 runs the CharaChorder OS, a closed-source project with only a
restricted set of chording configurations, and the fact that it must

主要讨论点：关于存档网站（archive.today）的有效性、道德性及其在保存网络内容方面的作用。

不同观点：

• **支持存档网站的观点**：
  - 认为存档网站（archive.today）在保存网络内容方面起到了重要作用，尤其是在原文可能被删除或更改的情况下。
  - 提供存档链接有助于保持信息的透明度和可追溯性，对研究和引用有帮助。
  - 例子：新闻文章或社交媒体帖子被删除后，存档网站可以作为历史记录供公众查阅。

• **质疑存档网站道德性的观点**：
  - 担忧存档网站可能侵犯版权，因为其未经原创作者或发布平台的许可复制内容。
  - 认为存档网站可能会被用于恶意目的，如传播错误信息或断章取义，因为存档内容可能脱离原始上下文。
  - 例子：有人可能会利用存档链接来恶意引用或误导他人。

• **对存档网站技术能力的观点**：
  - 支持者指出存档网站具有强大的技术能力，能够快速保存网页内容，并且在访问原网页受限时提供替代方案。
  - 批评者则认为存档网站的保存技术并不完美，某些动态内容或多媒体元素可能无法完整保存，从而影响信息的完整性。

• **关于存档网站使用便捷性的观点**：
  - 一些用户认为存档网站界面友好，操作简便，能够轻松创建和分享存档链接。
  - 另一方意见指出，存档网站的可用性受限，某些地区或网络环境下可能无法访问存档内容，影响其实用性。

补充讨论：

- 争议焦点在于存档网站在信息保存和版权保护之间的平衡，以及如何防止存档内容被滥用。
- 讨论还涉及到存档网站在不同法律框架下的合法性问题，尤其是在涉及国际版权法时。
- 有用户建议存档网站应与内容原创平台合作，以获得合法授权，从而避免法律和道德争议。

总结来看，评论中关于存档网站的讨论主要集中在信息保存的重要性、版权和道德问题、技术能力及其使用便捷性等几个方面。这些观点反映了用户对信息自由流动与知识产权保护之间矛盾的关注。

During World War II, German soldiers loot a Botticelli from Florence.
The Art of Deceit
July 26, 2025
Reading Time: 9 minutes
I
was introduced to Jimmy—I never learned his surname—during a visit to Athens in 2005. I was told that he had dozens of artworks, all of which he wanted to sell, but he wanted it to be utterly confidential. It seemed unlikely, but as I’ve learned from years in the business, it’s important to follow every lead; you never know where the next deal will come from. I was driven to Jimmy’s house in the suburbs of Athens. The gate opened, and at the end of the driveway, in gray sweats, stood Jimmy, puffing on a cigar. After insisting on complete discretion, he let me in.
The first thing I saw was a Cézanne landscape.

The Digital Antiquarian
A history of computer entertainment and digital culture by Jimmy Maher
Home
About Me
Ebooks
Hall of Fame
Table of Contents
RSS
