data.title: AI is a floor raiser, not a ceiling raiser
data.author: jjfoooo4
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了人工智能（AI）对学习曲线和不同领域的影响。AI可以根据学习者的水平提供个性化资源，解决传统学习资源不匹配的问题，从而重塑学习曲线。然而，AI在高级或争议性话题上的作用有限，因为其训练数据可能不足或包含矛盾信息。此外，AI可能被用于作弊，但长期来看作弊者难以成功。

技术变革带来不均衡的影响。在编程领域，AI对管理层帮助较大，但对处理复杂代码库的开发者帮助有限。在创意领域，尽管AI能生成内容，但由于创意行业竞争激烈且需要新颖性，AI生成的作品难以取代优秀的人类创作。

最后，AI对已有专用应用程序的任务（如电子邮件和食物 ordering）影响较小，因为现有产品已高度优化，AI的摘要功能在此类任务中作用有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（特别是LLM，如GPT等）在实际应用中的效果、其对不同人群能力的影响以及其在编程和工程领域的适用性。

不同观点：
• **AI增加不平等**：gruez认为，尽管博客中的图表看似客观，但实际与最近的研究结果相反，AI的使用增加了不平等，而非减少它。他引用了《经济学人》的文章作为支持。
• **AI对编程和原型开发的影响**：stillpointlab提到Andrew Ng的观点，强调在AI创业中，快速原型开发（Rapid Prototyping）比在现有代码库上改进更有效。这类似于从VM到容器的转变，新的编码方式可能让LLM更具生产力。
• **LLM的局限性**：LeftHandPath指出，LLM在处理复杂问题（如完整棋局）时表现不佳，用户需要清楚知道哪些问题适合问LLM。LLM可能会给出错误但看似合理的答案，这可能误导用户。
• **AI对新手和专家的不同影响**：manmal认为，AI对新项目（greenfield projects）的帮助大于对现有项目的改进，因此新手可能从中获益更多。而专家则需处理AI无法胜任的部分。
• **AI是插值器而非外推器**：amelius指出，AI擅长在已有的知识范围内工作，但不擅长进行创新或突破性思考。
• **AI的有效使用依赖于用户的引导能力**：conartist6和falcor84认为，AI的输出质量取决于用户是否能有效引导它。通过不断调整和优化提示，用户可以获得比初始输出更好的结果。
• **AI提高下限但不一定提高上限**：avbanks和sabakhoj认为，AI可以帮助新手快速入门，但对于领域专家来说，AI未必能显著提高其能力上限。
• **AI适用于原型设计但不适合工程**：godelski强调，AI在快速生成概念验证（PoC）方面表现优异，但在处理复杂工程问题时缺乏深度和广度。
• **AI导致平庸化**：bfigares和resters担心，AI可能导致各行业产出趋于平庸，因为新一代可能不再发展分析和写作等技能。

补充讨论：
• **AI的有效性依赖于用户的评估能力**：PeterStuer指出，AI的帮助效果取决于用户是否具备足够的专业知识来评估和验证其输出。对于已知领域，AI的帮助更大。
• **对无干扰环境的期待**：fellowniusmonk期待一个无干扰的操作系统，能帮助用户专注于思考和工作，而不是被广告和社交媒体分心。

争议焦点：
• **AI是否真正提高用户能力**：一些人认为AI帮助用户更快上手新领域，但也有人担心AI会导致平庸化，并让用户依赖于其输出的“看似正确”的信息。
• **AI在工程中的适用性**：一方认为AI可以加速原型开发和提高生产力，另一方则认为AI在处理复杂工程问题时缺乏深度。

44747634.article_content:
AI is a Floor Raiser, not a Ceiling Raiser
¶
A reshaped learning curve
¶
Before AI, learners faced a matching problem: learning resources have to be created with a target audience in mind. This means as a consumer, learning resources were suboptimal fits for you:
You're a newbie at
$topic_of_interest
, but have knowledge in related topic
$related_topic
. But finding learning resources that teach
$topic_of_interest
in terms of
$related_topic
is difficult.
To effectively learn
$topic_of_interest
, you really need to learn prerequisite skill
$prereq_skill
. But as a beginner you don't know you should really learn
$prereq_skill
before learning
$topic_of_interest
.
You have basic knowledge of
$topic_of_interest
, but have plateaued, and have difficulty finding the right resources for
$intermediate_sticking_point
Roughly, acquiring mastery in a skill over time looks like this:
What makes learning with AI groundbreaking is that it can
meet you at your skill level
. Now an AI can directly address questions at your level of understanding, and even do rote work for you. This changes the learning curve:
Mastery: still hard!
¶
Experts in a field tend to be more skeptical of AI. From
Hacker News
:
[AI is] shallow. The deeper I go, the less it seems to be useful. This happens quick for me. Also, god forbid you're researching a complex and possibly controversial subject and you want it to find reputable sources or particularly academic ones.
This intuitively makes sense, when considering the data that AI is trained on. If an AI's training corpus has copious training data on a topic that all more or less says the same thing, it will be good at synthesizing it into output. If the topic is too advanced, there will be much less training data for the model. If the topic is controversial, the training data will contain examples saying opposite things. Thus, mastery remains difficult.
Cheating
¶
The introduction of
OpenAI Study Mode
hints at a problem: Instead of having an AI teach you, you can just ask it for the answer. This means cheaters will plateau at whatever level the AI can provide:
Cheaters, in the long run, won't prosper here!
The impact of the changed learning curve
¶
Technological change is an ecosystem change: There are winners and losers, unevenly distributed. For AI, the level of impact is determined by
the amount of mastery needed to make an impactful product
:
Coding: A boon to management, less so for large code bases
¶
When trying to code something, engineering managers often run into a problem: They know the principles of good software, they know what bad software looks like, but they don't know how to use
$framework_foo
. This has historically made it difficult for, as an example, a backend EM to build an iPhone app in their spare time.
With AI, they are able to quickly learn the basics, and get simple apps running. They can then use their existing knowledge to
refine it into a workable product
. AI is the difference between their product existing or not existing!
For devs working on large, complex code bases, the enthusiasm is more muted. AI doesn't have context on the highly specific requirements and existing implementations to contend with, and is less helpful:
Creative works: not coming to a theater near you
¶
There is considerable angst about AI amongst creatives: will we all soon be reading AI generated novels, and watching AI generated movies?
This is unlikely because creative fields are
extremely competitive
, and beating competition for attention requires
novelty
. While AI has made it easier to generate images, audio, and text, it has (with
some exceptions
) not increased production of ears and eyeballs, so the bar to make a competitive product is too high:
Novelty
is a hard requirement for successful creative work, because humans are extremely good at detecting when something they are viewing or reading is derivative of something they've seen before. This is why, while Studio Ghibli style avatars briefly took over the internet, they have not dented the cultural position of Howl's Moving Castle.
Things you already do with apps on your phone
1
: minimal impact
¶
One area that has
not
seen much impact is in tasks that already have specialized apps. I'll focus on two examples with abundant MCP implementations: email and food ordering. AI Doordash agents and AI movie producers face the same challenge: the bar for a new product to make an impact is already very high:
Email would seem like a ripe area for disruption by AI. But modern email apps already have a wide variety of filtering and organizing tools that tech savvy users can use to create complex, personalized systems for efficiently consuming and organizing their inbox.
Summarizing
is a core AI skill, but it doesn't help much here:
Spam is already quietly shuffled into the Spam folder. A summary of junk is, well,
junk
.
For important email, I don't
want

44747634.article_summary:
本文讨论了人工智能（AI）对学习曲线和不同领域的影响。AI可以根据学习者的水平提供个性化资源，解决传统学习资源不匹配的问题，从而重塑学习曲线。然而，AI在高级或争议性话题上的作用有限，因为其训练数据可能不足或包含矛盾信息。此外，AI可能被用于作弊，但长期来看作弊者难以成功。

技术变革带来不均衡的影响。在编程领域，AI对管理层帮助较大，但对处理复杂代码库的开发者帮助有限。在创意领域，尽管AI能生成内容，但由于创意行业竞争激烈且需要新颖性，AI生成的作品难以取代优秀的人类创作。

最后，AI对已有专用应用程序的任务（如电子邮件和食物 ordering）影响较小，因为现有产品已高度优化，AI的摘要功能在此类任务中作用有限。
44747634.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI（特别是LLM，如GPT等）在实际应用中的效果、其对不同人群能力的影响以及其在编程和工程领域的适用性。

不同观点：
• **AI增加不平等**：gruez认为，尽管博客中的图表看似客观，但实际与最近的研究结果相反，AI的使用增加了不平等，而非减少它。他引用了《经济学人》的文章作为支持。
• **AI对编程和原型开发的影响**：stillpointlab提到Andrew Ng的观点，强调在AI创业中，快速原型开发（Rapid Prototyping）比在现有代码库上改进更有效。这类似于从VM到容器的转变，新的编码方式可能让LLM更具生产力。
• **LLM的局限性**：LeftHandPath指出，LLM在处理复杂问题（如完整棋局）时表现不佳，用户需要清楚知道哪些问题适合问LLM。LLM可能会给出错误但看似合理的答案，这可能误导用户。
• **AI对新手和专家的不同影响**：manmal认为，AI对新项目（greenfield projects）的帮助大于对现有项目的改进，因此新手可能从中获益更多。而专家则需处理AI无法胜任的部分。
• **AI是插值器而非外推器**：amelius指出，AI擅长在已有的知识范围内工作，但不擅长进行创新或突破性思考。
• **AI的有效使用依赖于用户的引导能力**：conartist6和falcor84认为，AI的输出质量取决于用户是否能有效引导它。通过不断调整和优化提示，用户可以获得比初始输出更好的结果。
• **AI提高下限但不一定提高上限**：avbanks和sabakhoj认为，AI可以帮助新手快速入门，但对于领域专家来说，AI未必能显著提高其能力上限。
• **AI适用于原型设计但不适合工程**：godelski强调，AI在快速生成概念验证（PoC）方面表现优异，但在处理复杂工程问题时缺乏深度和广度。
• **AI导致平庸化**：bfigares和resters担心，AI可能导致各行业产出趋于平庸，因为新一代可能不再发展分析和写作等技能。

补充讨论：
• **AI的有效性依赖于用户的评估能力**：PeterStuer指出，AI的帮助效果取决于用户是否具备足够的专业知识来评估和验证其输出。对于已知领域，AI的帮助更大。
• **对无干扰环境的期待**：fellowniusmonk期待一个无干扰的操作系统，能帮助用户专注于思考和工作，而不是被广告和社交媒体分心。

争议焦点：
• **AI是否真正提高用户能力**：一些人认为AI帮助用户更快上手新领域，但也有人担心AI会导致平庸化，并让用户依赖于其输出的“看似正确”的信息。
• **AI在工程中的适用性**：一方认为AI可以加速原型开发和提高生产力，另一方则认为AI在处理复杂工程问题时缺乏深度。

data.title: Fast
data.author: gaplong
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了软件速度的重要性，尽管在需求中很少被提及。快速的软件能改变行为，如开发者更频繁地发布代码、AI辅助编程加快原型制作、实时流支持远程工作等。反之，缓慢的软件会限制效率，比如在飞机WiFi下工作效率低下。快速软件消除了认知摩擦，显得神奇且简单，因为它迫使产品聚焦并去除不必要的功能。实现快速常需后台复杂处理，如Instagram优化照片上传。速度不仅是一项技术成就，还体现了优先级和专注。此外，快速也带来乐趣，并相对提升工作效率。未来，随着对性能和体验的关注增加，软件将解锁更多新功能和应用场景，改变生活。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软件开发和使用中的“速度”问题及其重要性

不同观点：
• PaulHoule：认为LLM（大型语言模型）辅助的工作流有时并不快，尤其是在“代理型”助手的情况下，完成任务需要很长时间。他分享了一次使用代理助手编写HTTP端点的经历，尽管初期提高了效率，但后续需要手动修改和优化，最终花费了更多时间。
• old-gregg：分享了一个职业早期关于速度的经历，强调速度在某些情况下可以直接带来经济效益。他还提到，虽然“快”不常被明确要求，但它是默认的期望。
• 9rx：指出虽然软件开发中很少有人明确要求“快”，但速度是赢得用户关注的关键因素，比如Rust语言因其比C++更快而受到关注。
• jodrellblank：通过Casey Muratori的例子说明，很多软件的性能可以通过简单的优化大幅提升，而不是依赖复杂的抽象和算法。
• hn_throwaway_99：感谢Hacker News界面的速度，并对比了Slashdot因界面改版导致的速度下降，最终失去了用户。
• ilyakaminsky：强调在云计算时代，速度直接关系到成本和利润，通过优化可以降低成本并提高服务质量。
• nu11ptr：认为“快”不仅仅是原始吞吐量，更重要的是“感知速度”。比如，Go语言的编译速度让人感觉很快，而Java的启动速度慢则让人感觉慢。
• SatvikBeri：指出速度的提升不仅在于完成相同任务更快，而在于可以改变工作流程，提高生产力。
• zavg：通过Pavel Durov的例子说明，应用的速度对用户行为有积极影响，Telegram和VK都因其速度快而受到用户欢迎。
• nakedneuron：强调速度不仅在于软件的响应速度，还在于用户操作的流畅度，比如使用键盘快捷键比使用鼠标更高效。
• kristianp：提到Google搜索的速度是界面速度的典范，而Microsoft的一些产品则显得慢。
• bravesoul2：认为性能问题通常是在问题出现后才被重视，建议通过良好的可观察性和定期的性能讨论来提前发现和解决问题。
• Aurornis：认为速度一直是用户体验的重要指标，尤其是在用户界面的响应速度和页面加载速度上。
• calibas：指出高效的代码不仅提升速度，还环保，减少电力消耗和硬件升级需求。
• chasing0entropy：认为当前行业更关注“可移植性”而非“速度”，导致软件性能下降。

补充讨论：
• 速度在不同场景下的重要性：从用户体验、经济效益到环境影响，速度被视为多个维度上的关键因素。
• 优化的方法：简单的代码优化和减少抽象层可以显著提升性能，而不一定需要复杂的算法。
• 感知速度 vs. 实际速度：用户对速度的感知有时比实际速度更重要，这影响到用户的体验和满意度。
• 速度与成本：在云计算和商业应用中，速度直接关系到成本和利润，通过优化可以实现更低的成本和更高的效益。

争议焦点：
• 对于“快”是否是默认期望存在不同看法。9rx和Aurornis认为速度是默认期望，而PaulHoule和old-gregg则认为虽然重要，但不一定总是被明确要求。
• 对当前行业是否忽视速度的看法不一。chasing0entropy认为行业更关注可移植性而忽视速度，而Aurornis则认为速度一直是重要指标。

44736967.article_content:
fast
Rarely in software does anyone ask for “fast.” We ask for features, we ask for volume discounts, we ask for the next data integration. We never think to ask for fast.
But software that's fast changes behavior.
Developers ship more often when code deploys in seconds (or milliseconds) instead of minutes.
AI code complete means we can prototype in languages we're less familiar with.
Real-time streaming makes remote work possible.
Conversely, slow software limits us more than we realize. When was the last time you used airplane WiFi and actually got a lot done? Maybe you sent a few Slack messages or answered a couple emails. Google Docs worked half of the time. You probably gave up. Instagram usually works pretty well—Facebook knows how important it is to be fast.
Fast is magical.
Fast eliminates cognitive friction. Raycast surfacing the right application before you finish typing feels like an extension of your mind. Superhuman's
sub-100ms
rule—plus their focus on keyboard shortcuts—changed the email game in a way that no one's been able to replicate, let alone beat. I recently used Mercury to pay another business that uses Mercury, and its instant settle felt surprising in a world where bank transfers usually take days.
No one praises these tools explicitly for their speed. They just feel magical.
Fast signals simplicity
, which is even rarer in a world where code and content are commodities.
Fast software has nowhere to hide. Network calls and dependencies reveal themselves through latency, and this brutal honesty forces discipline. Companies that do fast very well tend to have very focused products.
This is because the effort to make software fast often requires stripping away non-essential features. Compare how fast a streamlined project management tool like Linear loads versus an enterprise app like Workday (or worse… Oracle). In a world obsessed with adding rather than refining, speed becomes the ultimate expression of respect. It says, "We've thought deeply about what matters and eliminated everything else."
In order to make things fast, you often have to do complex things behind the scenes. At Cash App, we were very careful to only introduce additional steps in the user's journey when it was absolutely needed, which meant we had to handle a lot of messiness in the background. In
this interview
, Kevin Systrom explains how Instagram
optimistically uploaded
users' photos while they entered their caption to make the upload experience feel instant. Fast isn't just a technical accomplishment—it signals prioritization and focus.
Fast is fun
Also, we like fast because it's fun! We count WPM typing speeds for very little benefit except that it's fun to be faster than other people. The first thing we do on a new computer is set-up our hotkeys so we can go at the same speed as our last set-up.
Fast is relative
A lot of LLM-augmented workflows are infinitely faster than their pre-LLM counterparts today. Asking an LLM to research for 6 minutes is already 10000x faster than asking for a report that used to take days.
And yet, it's obvious to anyone that writes code that we're very far from the standards that we're used to from the previous software era. We're very focused on capabilities, and we're not very focused on performance or experience. We accept the clunkiness because the magic is still new, and that's ok! It's all still way faster than a human. But the current tools we have to build, run, and deploy AI apps feel very far off from the developer experience that we'll have in the future. We haven't yet begun the phase where optimization becomes the priority.
When we do, you'll see more and more companies optimizing for low latency, interface design, connectivity, and reliability.
This
, in turn, will unlock new capabilities and use cases that we aren't yet even thinking about. After all, the best software changes the way we live our lives, and we build our lives around software that feels like superpowers.
==
Some other pieces about fast that I've liked:
Patrick Collison
,
Charlie Marsh
,
Paul Graham
.
Edit: hi hn! If you liked this blog post, you'll love
www.onkernel.com
:)

data.title: Ethersync: Peer-to-peer collaborative editing of local text files
data.author: blinry
data.article_summary: Ethersync 是一个支持实时协作编辑本地文本文件的工具，适用于 pair programming 和笔记记录等场景，弥补了 Git 在实时协作方面的不足。它具有跨编辑器协作、显示同伴光标和选择、加密 P2P 连接、离线可用以及简单 JSON-RPC 协议扩展等功能。该项目正在积极开发中，支持 Linux、macOS 和 Android 平台，通过安装相应插件和命令行工具即可使用。用户可以通过分享和加入代码实现目录连接，实时同步文件更改。Ethersync 基于 Automerge、Iroh 和 Magic Wormhole 技术，遵循 AGPL-3.0 开源协议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕项目许可、协作功能、技术实现及应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• **关于开源许可的看法**：
   - [kruffalon] 认为使用AGPL或GPL许可证表明开发者真正关心他们的工作和世界，而不仅仅是等待风投。虽然MIT等其他许可也不错，但AGPL/GPL更具情怀。
   - 其他人没有直接回应这一观点，但讨论主要集中在技术实现上。

• **关于协作功能的看法**：
   - [xpe] 提到Zed编辑器的协作功能（如编辑和语音）是其早期宣传的亮点，并质疑有多少用户长期使用这些功能。
   - [dtkav] 分享了受Zed启发而开发的类似项目Relay，并提到使用yjs等技术，计划将其实现为“超级节点”。
   - [riedel] 认为“git的补充”是一个很好的价值主张，但要替代Google Docs或Overleaf还有很长的路要走，尤其是在与GitLab等平台的集成方面。

• **关于技术实现的讨论**：
   - [mentalgear] 对新的本地优先库和工具表示赞赏，并询问与y.js或automerge的比较。
   - [ethan_smith] 关心Ethersync是否使用CRDTs来解决冲突，还是采用其他方法。
   - [majkinetor] 对项目能在浏览器外使用表示赞赏，并希望支持更多操作系统。

🍃 Ethersync
Multiplayer mode for your text editor!
Ethersync enables real-time collaborative editing of local text files. You can use it for pair programming or note-taking, for example. It's the missing real-time complement to Git!
Features
👥 Edit files at the same time, across different text editors
📍 See your peers' cursors and selections
🗃️ Work on entire projects, the way you're used to
🔒 Encrypted peer-to-peer connections, no need for a server
✒️ Local-first: You always have full access, even offline
🧩
Simple JSON-RPC protocol
for writing new editor plugins
🚦 Project status
The project is under active development right now. We use it every day, but there's still some
bugs
to be aware of.
📥 Installation
1. Install the
ethersync
command
Ethersync works on Linux, macOS, Android, and on the Windows Subsystem for Linux.
Binary releases
The
releases on GitHub
come with precompiled static binaries. Download one and put it somewhere in your shell's
PATH
:
x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
for Linux
universal-apple-darwin
for macOS
aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
for Android (use a terminal emulator like
Termux
)
Arch Linux
yay -S ethersync-bin
Nix
This repository provides a Nix flake. To put
ethersync
in your PATH temporarily, run:
nix shell github:ethersync/ethersync
Make sure to also have it in your PATH when you run the editors.
Via Cargo
cargo install ethersync
2. Install an editor plugin
Neovim
VS Code/Codium: Install the "Ethersync" extension from the marketplace
📖 Basic usage
In the directory you want to share:
$ ethersync share
To connect to you, another person can run:
ethersync join 5-hamburger-endorse
Peer connected: adfa90edd932732ddf242f24dc2dcd6156779e69966d432fcb3b9fe3ae9831ab
Another person, in a separate directory (also works on the same computer):
$ ethersync join 5-hamburger-endorse
Derived peer from join code. Storing in config (overwriting previous config).
Storing peer's address in .ethersync/config.
Connected to peer: 5e6b787fff79074735eb9b56939269100de1e37bc7f7a4d29c277cc24f7ee53d
The directories are now connected, and changes will be synced instantly. You can open text files (using editors with an Ethersync plugin), and start collaborating in real time! ✨
🎓 Learn more
Learn more about Ethersync in
the documentation
.
Watch a
10-minute talk
given at FOSDEM 2025.
Watch a (German)
1-hour talk
given at MRMCD 2024.

We'd love to receive your patches and other contributions! Small patches are very welcome as PRs. Before starting to implement a new big feature, please briefly
check in with us
so we can discuss how it fits in with our ideas for the project.
If you're interested in building new editor plugins, read the

.

data.title: Coffeematic PC – A coffee maker computer that pumps hot coffee to the CPU
data.author: dougdude3339
data.article_summary:
《COFFEEMATIC PC》是由艺术家Doug MacDowell创作的一个结合了复古游戏电脑和咖啡机的项目。作者在2024年冬天从旧货店购买了一台1980年代的通用电气（GE）滴滤式咖啡机，并对其进行改造，使其成为一台功能齐全的电脑，同时保留了咖啡机的冲泡功能。该项目利用咖啡机 brew 的热咖啡（"Java"）为电脑的中央处理器（CPU）降温，通过水泵将热咖啡在散热器和CPU之间循环。尽管这个过程看似危险，但电脑运行稳定，最终达到一种热平衡状态。

Coffeematic PC 的硬件包括2000年代中期的主板、CPU、内存和显卡，以及现代的SSD和Linux Mint操作系统。整个项目历时一个月完成，结合了旧电子设备和现代硬件。作者还提到了自2002年以来“咖啡机电脑”的演变历程，他是首个使用热咖啡作为冷却方法的人。

该项目还启发了名为“Sparklines”的艺术展览，展示了手工绘制的数据可视化作品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过CPU加热水来制作咖啡的项目及其相关技术与幽默讨论

不同观点：
• jfengel提出将水通过CPU加热至80°C，再通过额外加热器加热以达到泡咖啡的温度，但指出这可能对CPU不利，因为过高的温度对电子元件有害。
• yupyupyups以幽默方式回应，提到运行Electron应用可以使咖啡变冷，暗示Electron应用的资源消耗大。
• Lio设想将该项目扩展为通过AI判断用户想要的饮品，并提到“几乎但不完全是茶”的幽默说法，可能在调侃某些AI项目的不完美。
• Groxx表达了对项目本身的喜爱，认为这是人们真正需要的建设性项目。
• bitcrshr引用HTTP 418状态码（著名的“我是茶壶”笑话），暗示项目不会出现“茶壶”问题。
• zeta0134认为这个项目是一种有趣的“愚蠢”项目，并指出咖啡作为散热器的功能令人愉悦。
• bluelightning2k和nojs都以“Java兼容”和“Java标志有意义”来开玩笑，利用Java语言与咖啡的双关。
• iammrpayments担心管道材料的安全性，质疑用于加热和输送水的材料是否适合饮用。
• ghm2180提出一个创意设计，即通过带触觉反馈的按键控制CPU/GPU，并通过按键感知水温，增加用户体验。
• dabumere简单表达了对项目的喜爱，称其让自己微笑。
• 9front幽默地建议使用“Coffee Linux”操作系统，而不是“Linux Mint”，继续项目中的咖啡主题。
• happycube以玩笑方式建议未来将项目升级为使用更高性能的i7处理器，暗示当前项目性能较低。
• parlortricks进一步开玩笑，提到使用高性能显卡（1080ti）运行Furmark软件来煮鸡蛋和培根，将项目扩展到制作全套早餐。
• bongodongobob提到项目应支持RFC 2324（定义了“超文本咖啡壶控制协议”），以增加项目的幽默和技术深度。

补充讨论：评论中充满了幽默和技术双关，大多数评论以轻松的方式讨论技术可行性和项目扩展的可能性，同时涉及了对Java语言、Linux操作系统、高性能计算硬件等技术元素的调侃。争议的焦点并不明显，因为讨论主要是幽默和创意驱动，但iammrpayments对管道材料安全性的关注提出了一个实际问题。

44762880.article_content:
COFFEEMATIC PC
A coffee maker computer by Doug MacDowell artist
Sometime during winter 2024, I found myself at a thrift store. I was staring at rows of appliances,
wrapped in plastic and clinging to life, trying to answer one question: which of these is the right
chassis for a retro gaming computer?
Driving home, I took corners carefully, checking that the General Electric (GE) drip coffee maker I’d
chosen was safe in the backseat. The coffee maker's given name was Coffeematic.  Circa 1980,
it is boxy yet athletic – unfazed by any considerations of future internet connectivity. Best, it is perfect for being hacked.
Coffeematic is now Coffeematic PC – part gaming computer, part coffee maker.
A newly synthesized machine percolating processes well beyond its original configuration.
Coffeematic PC is part of a lineage of coffee maker computers made since 2002
.
I'll describe that fascinating lineage here, and how it inspired an art exhibition called
Sparklines
where hand-drafted data visualizations accompany Coffeematic PC.
Profound and poetically articulated. Elegant and assertive. Highly scaleable with dynamic acceleration.
No. These do not describe Coffeematic PC or its peers (one of those phrases describes a bottle of wine.)
A custom built computer can be basic and functional, or an
elaborate, absurd,
spinning piece of art.
Coffeematic PC falls somewhere in that spectrum
while also being nearly self-destructive.
This is how Coffeematic PC works.
The computer is fully functional. The coffee maker is too
,
it percolates Java like a regular coffee maker. Very hot Java.
Computers usually use fans or liquid cooling systems to reduce heat.
Coffeematic PC uses the hot Java it brews to heat? cool? caffeinate? the computer.
A pump takes the hot, caffenated slurry (~90C/194F)
and circulates it thru two radiators sitting on top of Coffeematic PC's crown ->
down to a central processing unit (CPU) tucked within an ASUS M2NPV-VM
motherboard snugly strapped to Coffeematic PC's back.
Java continues through an artery returning to Coffeematic PC's caraffe.
The process repeats until Java is integrated with the user or the machine is powered off.
↑ Coffeematic PC has a dedicated pump to aggressively dispense Java for user.
CPU's are meant to be cool and Java hot.
Despite circulating hot Java,
Coffeematic PC does not crash.
To understand more, I wrote command line code to gather data on Coffeematic PC every 5 seconds,
and monitored Coffeematic PC for 75 minutes.
The graph below shows the results.
The machine is just barely non-destructive.
Coffeematic PC's CPU, body,
and circulatory system eventually find equilibrium. A warm 33C/91F -
amazingly close to the temperature of the slurry that flows through you and me.
An important part of this project is the lineage of coffee maker computers.
Before discussing that,
this is how Coffeematic PC was made.
The build is a mix of discarded electronics and newly purchased
hardware, pumps, and radiators. The motherboard, CPU, RAM, and graphics card are from the mid 2000's and were
sourced from a recycling center. This is a parts list for Coffeematic PC.
GE Coffeematic Coffee Maker 10 Cup
ASUS M2NPV-VM AM2 Motherboard
AMD Athlon II X4 640 3 GHz Quad-Core OEM/Tray Processor
Hynix 1GB 2Rx8 PC2-5300U-555-12 PC2-DDR2 RAM
Acer SA100 240 GB 2.5" Solid State Drive
HIS H467QR1GH Radeon HD 4670 1 GB Video Card
Antec Earthwatts Green 430 W 80+ Bronze Certified ATX Power Supply
Linux Mint Operating System
CPU Water Cooling Block for Intel
Water Cooling Computer Radiator
12V Mini Food Grade Self Priming Diaphragm Fresh Water Transfer Pump
Waterproof Toggle Switch 12V
Brass Hose Barb  3/8" to 3/16"
Brass Hose Barb, 5/16" to 3/16"
90 Degree Elbow Hose Barb 3/16"
90 Degree Elbow Hose Barb 3/8" 10mm
90 Degree Elbow Hose Barb 5/16" 8mm
Food Grade Silicon Tubing 3/16" ID x 5/16" OD
Food Grade Vinyl Tubing 5/16" ID - 7/16" OD
I spent about a month designing and building Coffeematic PC with the help from my beautiful fiance.
The build traverses time
. The coffee maker is from the late 1970's, the motherboard, CPU, and graphics card from the 2000's, and
the SSD, operating system, and hardware from the today's (2020's). The General Electric coffee maker needed only a minor repair of
replacing a small vinyl tube that had cracked. It takes awhile to brew a pot of coffee, but once it is brewed... it tastes like
coffee made from a plastic coffee maker from the 1970's. I'lllll drink it!
Video: Making a Coffee Maker Computer
A few clips of how Coffeematic PC was built.
Watch on YouTube
The lineage of coffee maker computer builds spans
22 years with a curious 15 year gap in the middle.
I'm not the first person to synthesize a coffee maker and a computer.
But, I think I am the first to use hot Java as a cooling method. The graph below shows the lineage of
coffee maker computers. There are a total of 5.  In 2002 Nick Pelis built the first ever coffee maker computer named
The Caffeine Machine
.

data.title: Weather Model based on ADS-B
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者使用RTL-SDR接收ADS-B消息，以构建简易气象模型的过程。ADS-B消息由飞机广播，包含位置、航向、速度等信息，任何人都可以通过天线和接收器获取。作者利用软件解码消息，并参考Junzi Sun的论文，通过分析飞机的地速、空速、航向和轨迹角，计算风速矢量，从而建立风模型。作者使用ADS-B Exchange的历史数据进行测试，将收集的数据在网格上模拟，通过随机游走更新粒子，最终生成风速可视化图。尽管模型在夜间数据较少时精度较低，但与真实气象数据对比，结果相当接近，验证了模型的有效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用航空器数据改进天气预报及相关技术应用

不同观点：
• sixdimensional：提到Flyht收购Panasonic Weather Solutions的资产，特别是TAMDAR传感器在商用飞机上的应用，这些传感器能够提供多层大气数据，在飓风路径预测方面表现出色。
• touisteur：建议使用飞机应答器的模式C（气压高度）与GNSS高度进行比较，以绘制大气压力图。
• antirez：讨论了dump1090的多个分支最终更名为readsb，指出新功能增加的同时，代码的简洁性和可理解性有所下降。
• NitpickLawyer：提到2017-2019年间Android手机的“未来几小时”天气预测非常准确，推测Google可能利用手机的气压传感器提高模型精度，并对之后准确性下降的原因进行猜测。
• birdlogic：询问获取的是飞机的实际航向还是地面轨迹推导出的数据，强调这对于计算风向的区别和重要性。
• MrGilbert：提到COVID期间天气预报准确性下降，可能是因为大量飞机停飞导致数据减少。
• throw0101d：建议类似技术是否可以应用于海洋自动识别系统（AIS）。
• therockspush：指出飞行计划通常提前提交，风数据可能过时，尤其在风切变情况下，飞行员报告对改善局部风事件预测非常重要。
• dceddia：认为这种天气产品对飞行员非常有用，并质疑是否已有类似产品，比如Sirius XM天气信息。
• yostrovs：纠正作者关于所有飞机必须安装ADS-B的说法，指出大多数通用航空并不要求安装。
• smath：对需要购买ADS-B接收器表示不解，因为adsb exchange已经汇总了所有数据。

补充讨论：
• chris_va：提供了与飞机传感器和风流相关的学术论文链接，供进一步参考。
• FL410和Havoc：对整个创意表示赞赏和肯定。

争议焦点：
• 天气预报准确性下降是否与COVID期间飞机停飞导致数据减少直接相关（MrGilbert的观点）。
• 利用手机气压传感器数据提升天气预测准确性的真实性及之后下降的原因（NitpickLawyer的观点）。
• 是否所有飞机必须安装ADS-B（yostrovs的纠正）。

44734515.article_content:
I recently bought an
RTL-SDR
dongle and an antenna to receive
ADS-B
messages. These are short packets of data, broadcast by every plane in the sky, to inform others of their position, heading, speed and other flight data. The transmission of these messages is mandatory for aircraft, as it prevents mid-air accidents.
They are also unencrypted, which means anyone can listen to them. All you need is an antenna and a dongle to ingest the data on your PC (pictured above), which can be bought for less than 100$. The incoming data can then be processed by software like
readsb
which decodes the messages.
You can choose to broadcast your own data to central servers like the
ADS-B Exchange
, like many hobbyists do. Thanks to them, we can visualise just about every aircraft currently in the sky. They also provide access to historic data.
One way these massive amounts of data can be used is to make cool visualisation, like
Clickhouse did
. We’re going to do something a bit different.
How does ADS-B Work
ADS-B messages are (usually)
transmitted by a mode S transponder
on the frequency 1090 MHz. Pulse position modulation is used to encode these messages as they transmit digital data (If you want to read about analog signal transmission, you can read my recent post on
FM radio
).
The excellent book
“The 1090 Megahertz Riddle”
by
Junzi Sun
goes into a lot of detail about ADS-B and how it works.
Collecting Data
By aggregating and processing the messages about position and heading, we can build a very crude meteorological model! All the work in this blog post is based on this
paper
(code available at
github.com/junzis/meteo-particle-model
).
ADS-B messages contain information about both ground speed (measured using a GPS) and airspeed (which is the plane’s speed relative to the surrounding air, measured by on-board sensors).
The ADS-B messages also contain the current heading and the track angle of the plane. The heading of the plane is direction the nose points in, while the track is the direction it moves in. These can diverge due to the wind shifting the plane from it’s actual course.
The difference between the vectors formed by (air speed, heading) and (ground speed, track) is the wind vector. By calculating this difference, we can infer wind speed at every point.
By combining this data from thousands of aircraft all over the sky we can build a little wind model that quite accurately simulates real wind conditions.
The paper by Junzi Sun also describes how to extract temperature and pressure from the data sent by the aircraft. By combining this with traditional meteorological models,
weather agencies can improve their forecasts
.
Building a Model
In order to test out the model, I first had to gather some data. After a quite measly run using my own antenna, I switched to
ADS-B Exchange’s historical data
. I pulled a total of 1.84 GB covering the 30th of April 2024.
Again, all credit goes to the authors of the paper, I only wrote some plumbing code to wrangle the data into a usable format and added some features to the visualisation for this blog post.
The model places the aircraft on a big grid. For each one, it spawns 300 particles scatter around it, which are initialised with the wind vector calculated for the aircraft. At each step, the particles are updated by a random walk.
To visualise the wind vectors, we need to measure the speed for each square of the map’s grid. To do this, we sample the particles for each square and take their average velocity vector. The more particles in a square, the higher the accuracy.
After letting the model run for a while, I got the following GIF - notice the outline of Europe in the background.
Each frame contains data from about 650 aircraft. The step size of the simulation was set to 15 minutes - which is quite a lot. The density plot visualises the accuracy - more aircraft, higher accuracy. As this is during the night, there is less activity, which results in less data for the model.
How Accurate is the Model?
While the wind vectors certainly do look interesting and somewhat realistic, are they really accurate? To compare the output of the simulation with real wind conditions, I found
Cameron Beccario
’s earth-wide wind visualisation.
Comparison between my model and
the reference model
powered by GFS.
The comparison is not exact, but it’s pretty close. I tried to match up the same countries in both images and the height of the aircraft in my model is about 11km while the data on the right is for 250 hPa (
nullschool.net
says 250 hPa corresponds to about 10,500m).
You can recognise the same high-speed winds over the Mediterranean (from Greece to Turkey), where the speed even matches up quite closely - our model predicting 50 m/s and the reference showing 152 km/h.
I’d say that’s a success!
I tried my best to replicate the style of the reference model to make a final visualisation.
My data visualised in the style of
earth.nullschool.net
.

data.title: Cerebras Code
data.author: d3vr
data.article_summary: Cerebras推出两款新计划——Cerebras Code Pro（50美元/月）和Code Max（200美元/月），旨在加速AI编码。两者均提供全球领先的开源编码模型Qwen3-Coder，速度达2,000 tokens/秒，上下文窗口为131k tokens，无专有IDE限制，也无每周限制。Code Pro适合独立开发者和小型工作流，每天可发送1,000条信息，支持3-4小时编码。Code Max则针对重度编码工作，每天可发送5,000条信息，适合全职开发和多代理系统。两计划均已开放，无需等待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Cerebras提供的Qwen3 Coder模型服务的性能、价格、限制以及与其他服务的比较。

不同观点：
• Flux159认为，Cerebras的服务虽然速度快，但因为不支持缓存，每次工具调用都需要发送整个消息历史作为输入 tokens，导致成本迅速上升。同时，质量不如Claude Code，但速度更快。
• Thanhhaimai指出宣传中的矛盾：尽管宣传中提到无每周限制，但细则中提到每天最多发送1000条消息，这让人难以认真对待。
• Crawshaw分享了他们的实验结果，发现Cerebras Code在Sketch中的表现由于过载问题不如他们托管的版本。
• Unraveller提到一些专业版用户报告的实际限制，例如每天750万tokens的限制，与广告不符。
• Alfalfasprout认为2k tokens/second的速度非常惊人，接近GitHub Copilot的水平，质量更好，对于编辑器内使用是颠覆性的。
• Namanyayg期待更多订阅服务竞争，认为这将有利于终端用户的价格。
• Ktsakas遇到了使用Claude-code-router和Qwen3 Cerebras时的API错误。
• Lvl155对Cerebras的硬件表示赞赏，但质疑为何没有更多投资者关注。
• Attentive指出Cerebras在处理"<think>"时的问题，在API和聊天中都被替换为"<tool_call>"。
• Deevus抱怨不同LLM服务的订阅模式不兼容，难以迁移数据。
• Sneilan1对Cerebras成为Claude Code的真正竞争对手感到兴奋，但对其高昂的价格和访问问题感到困扰。
• Clbrmbr认为Cerebras的定价应与Opus 4相比，而非Sonnet 4。
• Sophia01指出，用户可以修改编码代理以接入任何LLM提供商的API，但Cerebras似乎只通过高昂的月订阅提供Qwen3-Coder。
• Esafak建议直接托管所有最新的开源模型。
• Atkailash对在Cline中使用Cerebras的计划阶段表示兴奋。

补充讨论：
• 成本和缓存问题：Flux159和Unraveller都提到了成本和使用限制的问题。
• 速度和性能：Alfalfasprout和Thanhhaimai讨论了速度的优势以及宣传和实际限制之间的矛盾。
• 竞争和订阅模式：Namanyayg和Sneilan1期待更多竞争以改善用户体验和价格。
• 技术问题：Crawshaw、Ktsakas和Attentive分享了他们在使用中遇到的具体技术问题。
• 数据迁移和兼容性：Deevus和Sophia01讨论了不同服务之间的数据迁移和兼容性问题。

Aug 01 2025
Introducing Cerebras Code
Daniel Kim
We are launching two new plans designed to make AI coding faster and more accessible:
Cerebras Code Pro
($50/month) and
Code Max
($200/month). Both plans give you access to
Qwen3-Coder
, the world’s leading open-weight coding model—running at speeds of up to
2,000 tokens per second
, with a
131k-token context window
, no proprietary IDE lock-in, and no weekly limits!
Cerebras Makes Code Generation Instant
Even with the best frontier models, you still end up waiting around for completions. And as coding workflows get more agentic, the latency adds up fast. You’re not just waiting once. You have to wait on every LLM call across multi-step edits, tool use, retries, and planning.
At 2,000 tokens per second, code generation becomes instant. And starting at $50/month, anyone can use Cerebras Code and enjoy fast code generation that keeps you in flow.
Powered by a Frontier Model
Qwen3‑Coder is Alibaba’s flagship coding agent model. The 480B parameter model delivers performance comparable to Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT‑4.1 in coding and agentic tasks, achieving leading performance on coding benchmarks such as Agentic Coding, Agentic Browser-Use, and BFCL.
Bring your own AI IDE
If your code editor or tool supports OpenAI compatible inference endpoints, you can use it with Cerebras Code. Plug Cerebras Code into anything – Cursor, Continue.dev, Cline, RooCode, or whatever else you’re using. No extra setup. Just instant, high quality code generation inside your own workflow.
Available now
Cerebras Code Pro - ($50/month)
Qwen3-Coder access with fast, high-context completions.
Send up to 1,000 messages per day—enough for 3–4 hours of uninterrupted vibe coding.
Ideal for indie devs, simple agentic workflows, and weekend projects.
Cerebras Code Max - ($200/month)
Qwen3-Coder access for heavy coding workflows.
Send up to 5,000 messages/day.
Ideal for full-time development, IDE integrations, code refactoring, and multi-agent systems.
Cerebras Code Pro and Code Max are available today, no waitlist
. Sign up,
bring your key to your favorite editor, and start building instantly.
Get started today

data.title: Twentyseven 1.0
data.article_summary: Twentyseven 1.0.0是一个用Haskell编写的鲁比克方块解算器，是作者的早期项目之一，最初提交于2014年，2016年在Hackage上发布0.0.0版本。该项目源于作者对Haskell的兴趣，Haskell的惰性求值特性使其成为理想的选择。1.0.0版本主要是为了纪念，并使其能在当前GHC版本上编译。项目核心算法采用迭代加深A*（IDA*）搜索算法，以处理鲁比克方块庞大的状态空间。通过预计算和投影技术，IDA*能估算剩余步数，从而找到最短解法路径。尽管Twentyseven能找到最优解，但耗时较长。相比之下，Kociemba的两阶段算法速度更快，但非最优解。第一阶段将方块定向并分离边块，第二阶段限制移动以保持定向，从而在较小状态空间内快速求解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rubik's Cube主题的游戏项目及其技术实现

不同观点：
• [noduerme] 分享了自己开发的一款基于Rubik's Cube的比特币赌场游戏。该游戏的玩法是通过旋转立方体，并在限定时间内尝试解出尽可能多的三连匹配。他提到游戏的设计是基于技术（蒙特卡罗模拟）来确定赔率，并且理想玩家的期望值（EV）被设定为100%。他还指出，大多数玩家选择了更简单的版本，这个版本的期望值为92%。

• [andsoitis] 提到了一个名为Twentyseven的项目的实现，该实现基于Herbert Kociemba的Cube Explorer程序的笔记。他提供了该项目的源代码链接，并指出该项目是用Delphi（Object Pascal）实现的。

• [VoidWhisperer] 对原作者提出的一个问题进行了猜测，即为什么在每个面之间跳过第9个索引（例如，第一个面是00-08，下一个面从10开始到18，依此类推）。他认为这种方法可能是为了保持3x3网格中每个位置的数字一致性，其中X0代表左上角，X8代表右下角。

补充讨论：
• [noduerme] 的评论中提到了游戏设计中的技术细节，包括蒙特卡罗模拟和期望值的计算，展示了游戏设计的复杂性。
• [andsoitis] 提供了技术实现的参考资料，帮助理解如何使用特定编程语言（Delphi）来实现类似的项目。
• [VoidWhisperer] 提出了一个技术性的问题，并给出了自己的猜测，这引发了对数据结构和索引方式的讨论。

• 不同实现方法之间的选择（例如，为什么使用特定的索引方式，或者为什么选择Delphi作为开发工具）可能会引发关于效率和可维护性的讨论。

44763016.article_content:
Twentyseven 1.0.0
Posted on August  1, 2025
Twelve years of Haskell
Twentyseven
is a Rubikâs cube solver and one of my earliest projects in Haskell.
The first commit dates from January 2014, and version 0.0.0 was uploaded on Hackage in March 2016.
I first heard of Haskell in a course on lambda calculus in 2013.
A programming language with lazy evaluation sounded
like a crazy idea, so I gave it a try.
Since then, I have kept writing in Haskell as my favorite language.
For me it is the ideal blend of programming and math.
And a Rubikâs cube solver is a great excuse for doing group theory.
Twentyseven 1.0.0
is more of a commemorative release for myself,
with the goal of making it compile with the current version of GHC (9.12).
There was surprisingly little breakage:
Semigroup
has become a superclass of
Monoid
A breaking change in the Template Haskell AST
Aside from that, the code is basically just as it was 9 years ago,
including design decisions that I would find questionable today.
For example, I use
unsafePerformIO
to read precomputed tables
into top-level constants, but the location of the files to read from
can be configured by command-line arguments, so I better make sure that
the tables are not forced before the location is setâ¦
How Twentyseven works
The input of the program is a string enumerating the 54 facelets
of a Rubikâs cube, each character represents one color.
DDDFUDLRB FUFDLLLRR UBLBFDFUD ULBFRULLB RRRLBBRUB UBFFDFDRU
The facelets follow the order pictured below. They are grouped
by faces (up, left, front, right, back, top), and in each face
they are listed in top-down, left-right order.
00 01 02
03 04 05
06 07 08
10 11 12  20 21 22  30 31 32  40 41 42
13 14 15  23 24 25  33 34 35  43 44 45
16 17 18  26 27 28  36 37 38  46 47 48
50 51 52
53 54 55
56 57 58
The output is a sequence of moves to solve that cube.
U L B' L R2 D R U2 F U2 L2 B2 U B2 D' B2 U' R2 U L2 R2 U
The implementation of Twentyseven is based on Herbert Kociembaâs
notes
about
Cube Explorer
, a program written in Pascal!
The search algorithm is
iterative deepening A*
, or IDA*. Like A*, IDA* finds
the shortest path between two vertices in a graph.
A conventional A* is not feasible because the state space of a Rubikâs cube is massive (43 252 003 274 489 856 000 states,
literally billions of billions).
Instead, we run a series of depth-first searches
with a maximum allowed number of moves that increases for each search.
As it is based on depth-first search,
IDA* only needs memory for the current path,
which is super cheap.
IDA* relies on an estimate of the number of moves remaining
to reach the solved state. We obtain such an estimate by
projecting the Rubikâs cube state into a simpler puzzle.
For example, we can consider only the permutation of corners,
ignoring their orientation.
We can pre-compute a table mapping each corner permutation
(there are 8! = 40320) to the minimum
number of moves to put the corners back to their location.
This is a lower bound on the number of moves to actually solve a Rubikâs cube.
Different projections yield different lower bounds (for example, by
looking at the permutation of edges instead, or their orientation),
and we can combine lower bounds into their maximum,
yielding a more precise lower bound, and thus a faster IDA*.
Putting all that together, we obtain an optimal solver for Rubikâs cubes.
But even with these heuristics, Twentyseven can take hours to solve a random cube optimally.
Kociembaâs Cube Explorer is apparently much faster
(Iâve never tried it myself).
My guess is that the difference is due to a better selection of projections,
yielding better heuristics.
But I havenât gotten around to figure out whether Iâve misinterpreted
his notes or those improvements can only be found in the code.
A faster alternative is Kociembaâs two phase algorithm.
It is suboptimal, but it solves Rubikâs cubes in a fraction of a second
(1000 cubes per minute).
The first phase puts cubies into a âcommon orientationâ
and âseparatesâ the edges into two groups.
In other words, we reach a state where the permutation
of 12 edges can be decomposed into two disjoint
permutations of 4 and 8 edges respectively.
In the second phase, we restrict the possible moves:
quarter- and half-turns on the top and bottom faces,
half-turns only on the other faces.
These restricted moves preserve the âcommon orientationâ of edges and corners
from phase 1,
and the edges in the middle slice stay in their slice.
Each phase thus performs an IDA* search in a much smaller space
than the full Rubikâs cube state space (2 217 093 120 and 19 508 428 800
states respectively).
44763016.article_summary: Twentyseven 1.0.0是一个用Haskell编写的鲁比克方块解算器，是作者的早期项目之一，最初提交于2014年，2016年在Hackage上发布0.0.0版本。该项目源于作者对Haskell的兴趣，Haskell的惰性求值特性使其成为理想的选择。1.0.0版本主要是为了纪念，并使其能在当前GHC版本上编译。项目核心算法采用迭代加深A*（IDA*）搜索算法，以处理鲁比克方块庞大的状态空间。通过预计算和投影技术，IDA*能估算剩余步数，从而找到最短解法路径。尽管Twentyseven能找到最优解，但耗时较长。相比之下，Kociemba的两阶段算法速度更快，但非最优解。第一阶段将方块定向并分离边块，第二阶段限制移动以保持定向，从而在较小状态空间内快速求解。

data.title: Native Sparse Attention
data.author: CalmStorm
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为NSA（Native Sparse Attention）的稀疏注意力机制，旨在解决长上下文建模中的计算成本问题。NSA结合算法创新和硬件优化，通过动态层次化稀疏策略，在保持全局上下文感知和局部精度的同时，实现高效计算。其核心创新包括：平衡算术强度的算法设计和现代硬件优化，以及支持端到端训练以减少预训练计算量。实验表明，NSA在长上下文任务和指令推理中保持或超越了全注意力模型的性能，并在处理64k长度序列时显著加速。

View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Long-context modeling is crucial for next-generation language models, yet the high computational cost of standard attention mechanisms poses significant computational challenges. Sparse attention offers a promising direction for improving efficiency while maintaining model capabilities. We present NSA, a Natively trainable Sparse Attention mechanism that integrates algorithmic innovations with hardware-aligned optimizations to achieve efficient long-context modeling. NSA employs a dynamic hierarchical sparse strategy, combining coarse-grained token compression with fine-grained token selection to preserve both global context awareness and local precision. Our approach advances sparse attention design with two key innovations: (1) We achieve substantial speedups through arithmetic intensity-balanced algorithm design, with implementation optimizations for modern hardware. (2) We enable end-to-end training, reducing pretraining computation without sacrificing model performance. As shown in Figure 1, experiments show the model pretrained with NSA maintains or exceeds Full Attention models across general benchmarks, long-context tasks, and instruction-based reasoning. Meanwhile, NSA achieves substantial speedups over Full Attention on 64k-length sequences across decoding, forward propagation, and backward propagation, validating its efficiency throughout the model lifecycle.

data.title: Anthropic revokes OpenAI's access to Claude
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary: Anthropic 近日撤销了 OpenAI 对其模型（包括 Claude）的API访问权限，因 OpenAI 违反服务条款，利用 Claude 进行与其竞争的AI模型开发和测试。OpenAI 使用特殊开发者接口将 Claude 集成到内部工具中，以评估其在编码和安全提示方面的表现。Anthropic 表示将恢复 OpenAI 的部分API访问以进行行业标准的基准测试和安全性评估，但具体细节未明确。此类限制API访问的策略在科技行业并不少见，例如Facebook曾对Twitter旗下的Vine采取类似措施。这一事件发生在OpenAI即将发布更强大编码能力的新模型GPT-5之际。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI与Anthropic之间的API使用争议及竞争关系

不同观点：
• **[对API使用描述的质疑]** [luke-stanley] 认为Wired对OpenAI使用Anthropic的API描述过于夸张，实际上只是正常的API使用，而非“特殊开发者访问”。这种描述可能引起误解，让人以为OpenAI在进行不正当操作。
• **[对服务条款的批评]** [chowells] 指出Anthropic的服务条款中禁止用户使用其服务来构建竞争产品，这种限制让人不满，尤其是与没有使用限制的工具相比。
• **[对OpenAI行为的不同解读]** [ankit219] 认为OpenAI使用Anthropic的API是为了模型 benchmarking，但工具benchmarking则不被接受。Anthropic可能因为OpenAI试图对比其产品与Claude的性能而撤销了API访问权限。
• **[对Anthropic公关策略的看法]** [v5v3] 认为Anthropic允许OpenAI继续使用其API是一种公关策略，显示其产品的优越性，尽管OpenAI可以轻易地重新注册非官方账号。
• **[对竞争条款的双重标准批评]** [modeless] 引用OpenAI的服务协议，指出其同样禁止用户使用输出结果来开发竞争产品，认为这是“以其人之道还治其人之身”。
• **[对公司合作与竞争的看法]** [numbersense] 提到有传言说各大AI实验室私下合作，但不公开这些信息。
• **[对Anthropic行为的不满]** [Havoc] 认为Anthropic对OpenAI使用其API的描述是一种廉价的公关攻击，开发者使用API与训练模型是不同的概念。
• **[对公司行为的理解]** [Palmik] 认为每个AI公司都会使用其他公司的模型来进行评估，这是行业常态，Anthropic的做法让其形象受损。

补充讨论：
• **[技术问题与API使用体验]** [brokegrammer] 提到在使用过程中遇到的技术问题，并质疑文章是否夸大了事实。
• **[对AI聊天记录商业化的讨论]** [Buttons840] 提出了一种商业模式，即通过浏览器扩展付费获取用户的AI聊天记录，并讨论了这种做法的伦理问题。
• **[对Anthropic竞争策略的担忧]** [retinaros] 担心Anthropic的竞争策略过于激进，可能会对行业内的潜在竞争者采取不公平的措施，尤其是在AGI发展的背景下。
• **[对文章内容的批评]** [bethekidyouwant] 认为文章内容空洞，似乎是在为Anthropic打广告。

争议焦点：OpenAI是否通过API使用Anthropic的模型进行不正当竞争，以及Anthropic对此的反应是否合理。

Anthropic revoked OpenAI’s
API access to its models on Tuesday, multiple sources familiar with the matter tell WIRED. OpenAI was informed that its access was cut off due to violating the terms of service.
“Claude Code has become the go-to choice for coders everywhere, and so it was no surprise to learn OpenAI's own technical staff were also using our coding tools ahead of the launch of GPT-5,” Anthropic spokesperson Christopher Nulty said in a statement to WIRED. “Unfortunately, this is a direct violation of our terms of service.”
According to Anthropic’s
commercial terms of service
, customers are barred from using the service to “build a competing product or service, including to train competing AI models” or “reverse engineer or duplicate” the services. This change in OpenAI’s access to Claude comes as the ChatGPT-maker is
reportedly
preparing to release a new AI model, GPT-5, which is
rumored
to be better at coding.
OpenAI was plugging Claude into its own internal tools using special developer access (APIs), instead of using the regular chat interface, according to sources. This allowed the company to run tests to evaluate Claude’s capabilities in things like coding and creative writing against its own AI models, and check how Claude responded to safety-related prompts involving categories like CSAM, self-harm, and defamation, the sources say. The results help OpenAI compare its own models’ behavior under similar conditions and make adjustments as needed.
“It’s industry standard to evaluate other AI systems to benchmark progress and improve safety. While we respect Anthropic’s decision to cut off our API access, it’s disappointing considering our API remains available to them,” OpenAI’s chief communications officer Hannah Wong said in a statement to WIRED.
Nulty says that Anthropic will “continue to ensure OpenAI has API access for the purposes of benchmarking and safety evaluations as is standard practice across the industry.” The company did not respond to WIRED’s request for clarification on if and how OpenAI's current Claude API restriction would impact this work.
Top tech companies yanking API access from competitors has been a tactic in the tech industry for years. Facebook
did the same to Twitter-owned Vine
(which led to allegations of anticompetitive behavior) and last month Salesforce
restricted competitors
from accessing certain data through the Slack API. This isn’t even a first for Anthropic. Last month, the company restricted the AI coding startup Windsurf’s direct access to its models after it was rumored OpenAI was set to acquire it. (
That deal fell through
).
Anthropic’s chief science officer Jared Kaplan
spoke to TechCrunch
at the time about revoking Windsurf’s access to Claude, saying, “I think it would be odd for us to be selling Claude to OpenAI.”
A day before cutting off OpenAI’s access to the Claude API, Anthropic
announced
new rate limits on Claude Code, its AI-powered coding tool, citing
explosive usage
and, in some cases,
violations of its terms of service
.

data.title: JSON is not a YAML subset (2022)
data.author: AndrewDucker
data.article_summary: 文章主要指出，JSON并不是YAML的子集，因此不能安全地用YAML解析器来解析JSON。这会导致两种问题：JSON文档无法被YAML解析，或者被解析成语义不同的YAML结构。特别提到“挪威问题”，即YAML允许不加引号的字符串，导致意外结果。例如，YAML会将“NO”解析为布尔值false。此外，YAML 1.1和JSON在数字格式上也有差异，如YAML要求“1e2”写成“1.0e+2”。虽然YAML 1.2试图解决此问题，但JSON文档无法使用%YAML指令选择新版本解析方式，因此问题依然存在。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YAML与JSON的兼容性、YAML 1.1与1.2的差异、YAML与Unicode处理问题、YAML与XML的比较

不同观点：
• [pavel_lishin] 认为YAML 1.2的广泛采用与否并不重要，因为YAML解析器不能直接用于解析JSON文档。他质疑那些试图用YAML解析JSON的人的动机，称之为“假设的疯子”。
• [zzo38computer] 指出YAML 1.1和JSON在数字表示上的不同（如1e2在YAML 1.1中需要写成1.0e+2）。虽然YAML解析JSON有问题，但可以通过转换格式解决。他还提到，如果不需要兼容现有格式，可以选择其他格式如DER。
• [deathanatos] 讨论了YAML 1.2在Unicode转义处理上的不足，指出其在处理Unicode字符时缺乏明确规范，导致与JSON的不兼容问题。他提供了Python和Rust库的例子来说明不同语言处理上的差异。
• [sshine] 质疑YAML 1.1的广泛使用，认为YAML 1.2应该成为默认版本，从而避免不必要的YAML头部声明。他还指出JSON数字在实际语言实现中的复杂性，认为在处理科学计数法和大数时需要特别注意。
• [JonChesterfield] 强烈批评YAML的语法问题（如将 '[FI,NO,SE]' 解析为 ["FI", false, "SE"]），建议如果需要类似的功能，应该继续使用XML，认为XML在这方面更可靠。

补充讨论：
• YAML 1.1与1.2版本之间的差异引发了对数字和Unicode处理的不同看法。
• YAML的解析问题和复杂性被多位评论者提及，特别是与JSON和XML的对比。
• 争议的焦点在于YAML的兼容性和规范的明确性，尤其是在处理Unicode和数字格式时。
• 对于在何种情况下使用YAML、JSON或其他格式，不同评论者有不同看法，取决于具体需求和环境。

44762504.article_content:
JSON is not a YAML subset
People on the internet believe that JSON is a subset of YAML, and that it's safe to parse JSON using a YAML parser:
Following this advice will end badly because JSON is not a subset of YAML. It is easy to construct JSON documents that (1) fail to parse as YAML, or (2) parse to valid but semantically different YAML. The second case is more dangerous because it's difficult to detect.
False has over "1.7e3" named fjords
YAML (infamously) allows string scalars to be unquoted. A conforming YAML parser, presented with a token known to contain a scalar value, must match that token against a set of patterns and then
fall back
to treating it as a string. This behavior produces surprising outcomes, and has been named
The Norway Problem
.
@$ irb-3.1.2
require 'yaml'
@=> true
YAML.load '[FI,NO,SE]'
@=> ["FI", false, "SE"]
A similar issue affects JSON documents passed to a YAML parser when dealing with numbers in exponential notation. The YAML 1.1 spec is stricter about the syntax of numbers than JSON:
1e2
is a valid JSON number, but YAML 1.1 requires it to be written as
1.0e+2
. Being an invalid number, the YAML parser will treat it as a string.
@$ irb-3.1.2
require 'json'
@=> true
require 'yaml'
@=> true
JSON.load '{"a": 1e2}'
@=> {"a"=>100.0}
YAML.load '{"a": 1e2}'
@=> {"a"=>"1e2"}
YAML 1.2 won't save you
YAML 1.2 is a revision to the YAML spec that (among other goals) aims to make YAML a proper superset of JSON. To maintain backwards compatibility with existing YAML documents, the version is specified in a
%YAML
directive.
---
a: 1e2  # document["a"] == "1e2"
b: no   # document["b"] == false
%YAML 1.2
---
a: 1e2  # document["a"] == 100
b: no   # document["b"] == "no"
Regardless of whether YAML 1.2 has been (or will be) widely adopted, it does not help those who want to parse a JSON document with a YAML parser. JSON documents do not start with
%YAML
, and therefore cannot opt-in to the YAML parser behavior that would permit correct parsing of JSON.

data.title: Contrarian climate assessment from U.S. government draws pushback
data.author: WarOnPrivacy
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：气候变化报告的修辞策略及其背后的动机和影响

不同观点：
• [nxobject] 认为该报告采用了一种对抗性立场，通过挑选证据来支持其观点，然后声称这些观点在气候文献中未得到充分代表。这种策略依赖于受众本身对气候变化持怀疑态度。

• [gcanyon] 对“对抗性”立场持更激进的看法，认为这种“对抗性”实际上是“撒谎”，暗示报告中的立场不仅是挑拣证据，而且是故意歪曲事实。

• [chmod775] 持一种讽刺和幽默的态度，认为即使让小丑们发挥影响，也可以从中找到幽默，暗示对这种情况的无奈和接受。

• [Spivak] 认为科学家在拆解这些报告，但这也是一种“博士级”的内部争论，实际上是在浪费时间应对恶意误导的出版物。这些出版物被用来为既定决策提供借口，而作者本身并不相信其内容。同时指出，左派倾向于相信真相和事实可以战胜权力结构，这是一种被利用的弱点。

• [monero-xmr] 关注资助问题，质疑有多少联邦资金支持了与共识相反的实验室结果，暗示可能存在利益驱动的气候变化否定论。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于报告是否通过挑选证据来误导公众，以及这种策略是否故意为之。
• Spivak指出，这种报告的真正目的是通过制造科学探究的假象来分散注意力，避免挑战真正的权力结构。
• 讨论还涉及到应对气候变化的策略以及科学与权力结构之间的关系。

• decimalenough认为，猴子盗窃游客财物的行为背后存在一个人和猴子合作的三角犯罪体系。具体来说，猴子偷走游客财物后，寺庙内的祭司或看守人（即“猴子管理员”）通过用食物交换回物品，并借此获得游客的小费。这一观点强调了人类在猴子犯罪行为中的参与和获利。
• OutOfHere支持decimalenough的观点，并进一步指出，猴子是被它们的“人类训练者”教导进行这种盗窃行为的，目的是推动当地食品销售商的利益，属于一种人为策划的犯罪活动。
• bediger4000则提出了更为激进的看法，认为需要对参与这种行为的“犯罪家族”施以严厉惩罚，尽管这些猴子不会说话，但他们认为只有通过暴力和赎金的方式才能解决问题。

• thmryth和econ的评论带有戏谑成分，thmryth提到本以为讨论对象会是某家公司（如Sony、Bethesda或信用卡公司），而econ则开玩笑地问猴子是否能送饮料或包裹，这些评论偏离了主要讨论点，带有调侃性质。
• Detrytus分享了自己在直布罗陀的类似经历，提到那里的猴子会跳上车或偷走钱包，这为讨论提供了另一个地理背景下的相似案例。
• 其他如hatthew和damontal的评论较为简短且带有调侃性质，并未深入参与讨论。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于猴子盗窃行为是否完全自发，还是受到人类（如寺庙管理员或训练者）的教唆或利用。decimalenough和OutOfHere明确指出人类在其中的作用，而其他评论更多关注猴子行为本身或以幽默方式回应。

data.title: Meta dishes out $250M to lure 24-year-old AI whiz kid
data.author: haskellandchill
data.article_summary: Meta（Facebook母公司）以2.5亿美元的薪酬 package 招募了24岁的人工智能专家 Matt Deitke，突显了科技巨头在争夺顶尖AI人才方面的激烈竞争。Deitke原为华盛顿大学计算机科学博士生，后加入西雅图的艾伦人工智能研究所，领导开发多模态AI聊天机器人。他拒绝了Meta最初约1.25亿美元的offer，但在马克·扎克伯格亲自将offer加倍后接受。Deitke与人共同创立了AI初创公司Vercept，并获得了2022年NeurIPS杰出论文奖。尽管这种高薪酬激励了创新，但也引发了对经济不平等和权力集中的担忧，批评者认为这可能会加剧社会不公并导致大量工作岗位被AI取代。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta高薪聘请人才的合理性及道德性

不同观点：
• [brcmthrowaway] 表达了一种对人生方向的迷茫，虽然没有直接讨论主题，但引发了薪酬和职业选择的思考。

• [gedy] 认为与其高薪聘请一个人，不如雇佣250个有潜力的年轻人，每人支付100万美元的薪酬。他认为这样不仅能获得公关效果，还能带来更多实际价值。

• [warofwords] 提出Meta面临用户不再希望使用其更多服务的困境，并质疑高薪聘请“天才”来增加用户使用时间和注意力的道德性。他认为，除非有明显的用户生活改善结果，否则这250万美元的合同显得邪恶。

• [vivzkestrel] 质疑所谓“天才” kid的能力，认为他们能做的事情并没有特别之处，普通人也可以做到。

• [NHQ] 从通货膨胀的角度指出，250万美元在2025年其实只相当于2500万美元的购买力，认为这个薪酬并没有表面上看起来那么夸张。

- 争议的焦点在于高薪聘请单个天才是否比雇佣多个年轻人更有效，以及这种高薪是否会带来不良的社会影响。
- 不同观点之间的讨论关系显示出对高薪聘请合理性的不同理解和关注点。

44763714.article_content:
Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta gave a 24-year-old artificial intelligence whiz a staggering $250 million compensation package, raising the bar in the recruiting wars for top talent — while also raising questions about economic inequality in an AI-dominated future.
Matt Deitke, who recently dropped out of a computer science doctoral program at the University of Washington, initially turned down Zuckerberg’s “low-ball” offer of approximately $125 million over four years,
according to the New York Times.
But when the Facebook founder, a former whiz kid himself, met with Deitke and doubled the offer to roughly $250 million — with potentially $100 million paid in the first year alone — the young researcher accepted what may be one of the largest employment packages in corporate history, the Times reported.
4
Matt Deitke, the 24-year-old AI researcher who landed a $250 million deal with Meta, is at the center of Silicon Valley’s escalating talent war.
X / @mattdeitke
“When computer scientists are paid like professional athletes, we have reached the climax of the ‘Revenge of the Nerds!'” Professor David Autor, an economist at MIT, told The Post on Friday.
Deitke’s journey illustrates how quickly fortunes can be made in AI’s limited talent pool.

After leaving his doctoral program, he worked at Seattle’s Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence, where he led the development of Molmo, an AI chatbot capable of processing images, sounds, and text — exactly the type of multimodal system Meta is pursuing.
In November,
Deitke co-founded Vercept
, a startup focused on AI agents that can autonomously perform tasks using internet-based software. With approximately 10 employees, Vercept raised $16.5 million from investors including former Google CEO Eric Schmidt.
His
groundbreaking work on 3D datasets
, embodied AI environments and multimodal models earned him widespread acclaim, including an Outstanding Paper Award at NeurIPS 2022. The award,
one of the highest accolades in the AI research community
, is handed out to around a dozen researchers out of more than 10,000 submissions.
4
Deitke initially turned down Meta’s offer before CEO Mark Zuckerberg (pictured) doubled it to secure his move to the Superintelligence Lab.
REUTERS
The deal to lock up Deitke underscores Meta’s aggressive push to compete in artificial intelligence.
Meta has reportedly paid out more than $1 billion to build an all-star roster, including luring away Ruoming Pang,
former head of Apple’s AI models team
, to join its Superintelligence Labs team with a
compensation package
reportedly worth more than $200 million.
The company said capital expenditures will go up to $72 billion for 2025, an increase of approximately $30 billion year-over-year, in its earnings report Wednesday.
While proponents argue that competition drives innovation, critics worry about the concentration of power among a few companies and individuals capable of shaping AI’s development.
Ramesh Srinivasan, a professor of Information Studies and Design/Media Arts at UCLA and founder of the university’s Digital Cultures Lab, said the direction that companies like Meta are taking with artificial intelligence is “foundational to why our economy is becoming more unequal by the day.”
“These firms are awarding hundreds of millions of dollars to a handful of elite researchers while simultaneously laying off thousands of workers—many of whom, like content moderators, are not even classified as full employees,” Srinivasan told the New York Post.
4
Meta recruited Deitke with one of the largest known compensation packages in tech history, reportedly after a direct outreach from Mark Zuckerberg.
X / @Scobleizer
“These are the very jobs Meta and similar companies intend to replace with the AI systems they’re aggressively developing.”
Srinivasan, who advises US policymakers on technology policy and has written extensively on the societal impact of AI, said this model of development rewards those advancing large language models while “displacing and disenfranchising the workers whose labor, ironically, generated the data powering those models in the first place.”
“This is cognitive task automation,” he said. “It’s HR, administrative work, paralegal work — even driving for Uber. If data can be collected on a job, it can be mimicked by a machine. All of those forms of income are on the chopping block.”

Ruoming Pang, former head of Apple’s AI models team, was among the high-profile researchers reportedly poached by Meta.
LinkedIn / Ruoming Pang

data.title: Attendance at English football: a tale of tragedy and recovery
data.author: Vermin2000
data.article_summary:
这篇文章讨论了英格兰足球的观赛人数趋势及其背后的历史背景，特别是与足球流氓行为、种族主义、反犹主义和多次重大悲剧事件的关联。文章指出，自职业足球开始以来，英格兰足球一直受到足球流氓问题的困扰，20世纪80年代情况尤为严重，包括希尔斯堡惨案在内的多次灾难导致大量球迷死亡。同时，种族主义和反犹主义也在足球场上屡见不鲜。为应对这些问题，政府和足球管理机构采取了多项措施，如终身禁赛和全座位球场的引入，使情况逐渐改善。

观赛人数数据显示，20世纪80年代末 attendance 达到最低点，随后因各项改革和球场设施的改善开始回升。COVID-19疫情也对观赛人数产生了显著影响，2019-2021年间比赛多为空场进行。总体而言，尽管足球环境已大幅改善，但仍有许多工作需要继续推进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英格兰足球的负面问题，特别是从观众人数反映出的潜在问题。

• 隐含的观点是，有些人可能认为足球观众数量下降可能与比赛质量、俱乐部管理、球迷体验或社会经济因素有关，但具体原因尚未展开讨论。

补充讨论：
• 观众人数的变化被视为关键指标，用于揭示英格兰足球中可能存在的深层次问题。
• 该评论引导读者去查看具体的交互式数据，以更深入地理解观众人数变化的趋势及其背后的原因。
• 争议的焦点可能在于，观众人数是否是衡量足球"黑暗面"的最佳或唯一指标。有人可能认为其他因素（如球迷文化、俱乐部财政问题等）也同样重要。

总结：Vermin2000提出英格兰足球存在问题，并通过观众人数的变化来引发对此问题的关注和探讨，但具体原因和争议点尚未详细展开。

44763257.article_content:
Sport and on-going tragedy
Analyzing sports data is normally a harmless activity, but sometimes, it takes you to much darker places, and analyzing attendance in English football takes you to some dark places very quickly.
This blog post is about trends in attendance in English football and what you can tell from the data. For this analysis, I’m going to flip the script and start to talk about causes first and then show you the data.
(
Steenbergs from Ripon, United Kingdom
,
CC BY 2.0
, via Wikimedia Commons. Newcastle United vs. Chelsea, 2010-11-28. Note everyone seated and almost all seats filled.)
Hooliganism, racism, antisemitism, and tragedy
Football in the UK has suffered from hooliganism almost since the beginning of professional football. There are reports of riots dating back to 1909 and vandalism from 1934. After the Second World War, hooliganism arrived in earnest and by the 1980’s, the English game was in deep trouble. Notoriously, violence followed English teams abroad. Innocent people were caught up in the mayhem and were killed.
The UK government acted to crack down on offenders and the football authorities worked to make the game safer. Things improved slowly through the 1990’s, and the game’s battered reputation gradually improved and matches became safer to go to.
By the 1970’s, black players started to appear in English football teams, and so did racism. Some spectators threw banana peels on the pitch and make monkey noises when a black player got the ball. England ‘fans’ abused black English players at international matches. Perhaps unsurprisingly, hooligans had links to far right groups and were extremely racist.
The football governing bodies cracked down hard on racism and banned people for life from all stadiums, but of course, it’s still present.
As you might expect, antisemitism is also a problem. Tottenham Hotspur has a long and well-known connection with Jewish communities in London. So, opposing fans would regularly shout antisemitic abuse.
Sadly, to complete the picture, I need to point out some significant English horrors, only one of which (Heysel Stadium) was related to hooliganism.
1946 Burnden Park, Bolton Wanderers vs. Stoke City. 33 fans killed by crush injuries.
1985 Valley Parade, Bradford. Bradford City vs. Lincoln City. 56 spectators killed by fire.
1985 Heysel Stadium, Brussels. Juventus vs. Liverpool. 39 fans killed by a collapsing wall.
1989 Hillsborough, Sheffield. Liverpool vs. Nottingham Forest. 97 fans killed by crush injuries.
The Hillsborough disaster in particular triggered a series of wide-ranging changes, for example, the introduction of all-seater stadiums.
Given all this, would you take your children to a football match in the late 1980's or early 1990's?
You can read more on these issues here:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_hooliganism_in_the_United_Kingdom
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism_in_English_football
https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68478112
To sum it all up, the 1980’s were the nadir of English football. Things have got a lot better since then, but there’s work to be done.
Now, let’s look at the data.
Attendance numbers
The chart below shows total attendance by league for each year since the start of the league system in 1888. Total attendance is the sum of the attendance for each match held that season. The data is for English league matches only. The salmon-colored bands are World War I and World War II.
The chart is interactive, you can click on the legend to turn the leagues on and off, and you can use the toolbar on the right to zoom in and move around the data.
The chart shows the growth in attendance up to the immediate post-war period, followed by a decline. The nadir was 1989. I’ve explained above what was going on post-war, and given the issues, it’s no surprise attendance fell off.
The post-1989 recovery is probably due to a number of factors. The authorities have acted decisively to stamp out hooliganism, racism, and antisemitism. In the wake of the Hillsborough disaster, owners have invested in new stadiums that offer fans a much more pleasant experience. Fan culture has changed too, with more families attending matches and clubs actively trying to attract them. Notably, these changes are at all levels of the game.
COVID
COVID impacted the 2019-2020 season, with part of the season played behind closed doors and the lower leagues (tiers 3-5), cancelling games. However, the 2020-2021 season was played almost entirely without spectators. This is very clear in the attendance figures on the chart.
Home advantage
In a previous blog post, I used this chart below which shows the decline in home advantage (again, it’s interactive). One of my favorite explanations for home advantage was the effect of spectators. The key insight was that during COVID, home advantage (along with spectators), disappeared.
Sadly, there’s a problem. Compare the shape of this graph to the attendance graph above. The decline in home advantage has been

44763984.article_content:
Helsinki has not recorded a single traffic fatality in the past 12 months, city and police officials confirmed this week.
The city's most recent fatal accident occurred in early July 2024 on Keinulaudantie in the city's Kontula district.
Authorities are calling the situation exceptional.
"A lot of factors contributed to this, but speed limits are one of the most important," said
Roni Utriainen
, a traffic engineer with the city's Urban Environment Division.
Slower speeds, safer streets
According to Utriainen, more than half of Helsinki's streets now have a speed limit of 30 km/h. Fifty years ago, that proportion featured 50 km/h limits.
Earlier this summer, Helsinki decided to lower speed limits near schools to 30 km/h, a measure that is set to take effect as the academic year begins.
Smarter design and better enforcement
Street design has also played a key role. Pedestrian and cycling infrastructure has been significantly upgraded in recent years. In addition, cooperation with traffic police has intensified and more traffic cameras and automated enforcement systems have been introduced.
"Public transport in Helsinki is excellent, which reduces car use, and with it, the number of serious accidents," Utriainen noted.
Vehicle technology has also improved, making both cars and other personal transport options safer than ever.
The positive trend extends beyond fatalities. In the past year, there were 277 injury-causing traffic accidents in Helsinki — a sharp contrast to the nearly 1,000 injurious accidents recorded annually in the late 1980s, when traffic deaths in the city commonly approached 30 per year.
Long-term effort pays off
Helsinki's current traffic safety strategy, covering 2022–2026, is nearing completion. It has focused on improving safety for children, youth, pedestrians and cyclists with safer crosswalks and smarter intersection design.
Much of the planning has been data-driven, enabled by improved traffic monitoring tools.
Utriainen credited the improvement to decades of sustained effort.
"The direction has been positive for years," he said, pointing out that no pedestrians were killed in Helsinki traffic in 2019 either.
Traffic education has also improved, but Utriainen emphasised that credit belongs to everyone on the road — motorists, cyclists and pedestrians alike.
One newer challenge has been the widespread use of electric scooters.
"They became popular around five years ago, somewhat unexpectedly. But since then, many solutions have been put in place," Utriainen said.
The EU's long-term goal is zero traffic deaths by 2050 — a policy dubbed "Vision Zero." Is it achievable or wishful thinking?
"For us, it's more about how the goal guides our everyday actions," said Utriainen. "We aim to assess all our decisions based on their long-term impact."

data.title: The mathematics of starvation: how Israel caused a famine in Gaza
data.author: lr0
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了以色列如何通过控制进入加沙的食品供应，导致该地区出现饥荒。自2006年以来，以色列根据计算控制加沙居民的卡路里摄入，以避免他们饿死但同时保持饥饿状态。尽管人道主义组织要求每月向210万加沙居民提供至少62,000吨干粮和罐头食品，实际进入加沙的食品远低于最低需求。今年3月至6月，仅56,000吨食品获准进入，不到需求量的四分之一。尽管国际社会施压，以色列总理内塔尼亚胡仅承诺少量额外援助，饥荒仍在加剧。专家警告，加沙正面临“最坏情况”的饥荒，食品供应严重不足。

44763909.article_content:
Five-year-old Lana Salih Juha, who suffers from severe malnutrition.
Photograph: Mohammed Y. M. Al-yaqoubi//Anadolu via Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
Five-year-old Lana Salih Juha, who suffers from severe malnutrition.

Gaza
The mathematics of starvation: how Israel caused a famine in Gaza
Israel controls the flow of food into Gaza. It has calculated how many calories Palestinians need to stay alive. Its data shows only a fraction has been allowed in
Emma Graham-Harrison
Chief Middle East correspondent
Thu 31 Jul 2025 10.49 EDT
Last modified on Fri 1 Aug 2025 09.23 EDT
Share
T
he mathematics of famine are simple in Gaza. Palestinians cannot leave, war has ended farming and
Israel
has banned fishing, so practically every calorie its population eats must be brought in from outside.
Israel knows how much food is needed. It has been calibrating hunger in
Gaza
for decades, initially calculating shipments to exert pressure while avoiding starvation.
Children and elderly people most vulnerable as Gaza famine deepens, warn experts
Read more
“The idea is to put the Palestinians on a diet, but not to make them die of hunger,” a senior adviser to the then prime minister, Ehud Olmert,
said
in 2006. An Israeli court ordered the release of documents showing the
details
of those macabre sums two years later.
Cogat, the Israeli agency that still controls aid shipments to Gaza, calculated then that Palestinians needed an average minimum 2,279 calories per person per day, which could be provided through 1.836kg of food.
Today, humanitarian organisations are asking for an even smaller minimum ration: 62,000 metric tonnes of dry and canned food to meet basic needs for 2.1 million people each month, or around 1kg of food per person per day.
As Gaza has slid into famine this summer, Israeli officials have variously
denied
the existence of mass starvation, claimed
without
evidence
that Hamas steals and hoards aid, or blamed hunger on UN distribution failures, sharing pictures of aid pallets awaiting collection inside the border.
bar chart showing that more people in Gaza died of starvation in just over 11 days than in the previous 21 months of conflict
They pointed to
deadly and chaotic
food distributions by the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, a US and Israeli-backed logistics startup, as proof that Palestinians had access to food.
Yet data compiled and published by Israel’s own government makes clear that it has been starving Gaza. Between March and June, Israel allowed just 56,000 tonnes of food to enter the territory, Cogat records show, less than a quarter of Gaza’s minimum needs for that period.
How will the UK’s recognition of Palestine help those starving in Gaza? - podcast
Read more
Even if every bag of UN flour had been collected and handed out, and the GHF had developed safe systems for equitable distribution, starvation was inevitable. Palestinians did not have enough to eat.
A “worst-case scenario” famine is now unfolding in Gaza, UN-backed food security experts said this week. Food deliveries are “at a scale far below what is needed”, amid “drastic restrictions on the entry of supplies”, the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) said in a report citing Israeli figures on aid.
The
Famine
Review Committee, an independent group of experts that scrutinises IPC alerts, said food shipments “have been highly inadequate”, and singled out the GHF.
“Our analysis of the food packages supplied by the GHF shows that their distribution plan would lead to mass starvation, even if it was able to function without the appalling levels of violence that have been reported,” the FRC said.
In March and April Gaza was under total siege, with no food entering. In mid-May Netanyahu said shipments would restart because of international pressure over a “starvation crisis”.
View image in fullscreen
Data compiled and published by Israel’s own government makes clear that it has been starving Gaza.
Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images
Just a few weeks of extra aid shipments during the ceasefire in January and February this year provided enough calories to bring Gaza back from the brink of famine, UN data shows.
However, in May only a trickle of food returned, in quantities that served only to slow Gaza’s descent into starvation, not stop it. Two months on, the scale of suffering has now spurred another round of international outrage, including
demands
from Donald Trump to get “every ounce of food” to starving children.
chart showing that by Israel’s own figures, the amount of aid reaching Gaza falls well below subsistence levels
In response Netanyahu has promised only “minimal” extra aid. The number of food trucks entering the territory has risen, but is still well below the minimum needed to feed Palestinians there, much less reverse a famine.

Aid packages, dropped from a plane, descend into Gaza.
Photograph: Hatem Khaled/Reuters

Secure passwords
are the first layer of security for your online accounts, but they’re not enough on their own to keep you safe from data leaks and hackers.
That’s where your 2FA app comes in. Two-factor authentication adds a second layer of defense when logging in to your accounts. It’s a universally recommended way to keep your accounts secure.
Today we’re introducing Proton Authenticator, a free 2FA app that gives you more flexibility than other authenticators, along with strong encryption from a trusted team. Proton Authenticator is open source like all our apps, available for every device (including desktop!), and lets you import all your existing 2FA tokens in seconds.
Download Proton Authenticator
Proton Authenticator is available now for free on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
Redefining 2FA to give you more control
The increasing menace of account takeover attacks costs people and businesses
tens of billions of dollars
(new window)
every year. Unlike other kinds of cyber threats, this one is relatively simple to prevent — just enable 2FA on your accounts.
With 2FA, you’ll enter a second piece of information in addition to your password when logging in to an account. Typically that info is a six-digit code generated by your authenticator app. Even if someone has your password, they can’t gain access to your account. While SMS authentication codes are another common option, this leaves you vulnerable to
sim swapping attacks
. An authenticator app is much more difficult for hackers to crack because it generates codes locally on your device, and each code expires after 30 seconds.
While there are many 2FA apps available, the majority are closed source, rely on ads and trackers, and don’t offer end-to-end encrypted 2FA backups, making them a choice filled with compromise for the
Proton community
. Some of them don’t even support data export, so you are trapped forever in a bad app that might eventually disappear. We wanted to offer a no-compromise choice.

Access your 2FA codes on mobile and desktop apps, even offline.
Sync your 2FA codes to all your devices with end-to-end encryption.

Easily import from other 2FA apps, or export from Proton Authenticator.

open source

Proton Authenticator protects your accounts with best-in-class security for free, whether you have a Proton Account or not. Whether you manage dozens of accounts daily or need a high-security setup, Proton has a privacy-first, easy-to-use solution for you.

data.title: Corporation for Public Broadcasting says it's shutting down
data.author: divbzero
data.article_summary: 美国公共广播公司（CPB）宣布将在2025年9月30日关闭，因特朗普总统签署了一项取消所有联邦资助的法律。CPB是联邦资金流向NPR和PBS等公共媒体的中介，此次关闭是由于国会通过了一项撤销11亿美元公共广播资金的决议。尽管公众努力呼吁保留资助，但未果。CPB表示，大部分员工职位将在本财年结束时取消，少量团队将留任至明年1月处理后续事务。公共媒体机构对关闭表示震惊和悲伤，一些地方电台已开始裁员，而其他电台则收到大量捐款支持。NPR和PBS均否认偏见指控，并表示将继续支持地方公共媒体，维持高质量的新闻和文化节目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于是否应该在科技行业引入更多监管以保护消费者和社会的讨论。

不同观点：
• 支持加强监管的观点：
  - 认为科技公司在隐私、数据安全和市场垄断等方面对消费者和社会造成了实质伤害。
  - 举例：Facebook的数据泄露事件、Google的垄断行为等显示了科技公司缺乏自律。
  - 强调科技公司拥有过多的权力和影响力，需要通过外部监管来制衡。
  - 认为监管可以促进公平竞争，防止大公司通过不正当手段压制小型创新企业。

• 反对加强监管的观点：
  - 认为过度的监管会抑制创新，增加企业的合规成本，最终损害消费者利益。
  - 举例：欧洲的GDPR法规虽然保护了隐私，但也导致一些小型企业因合规困难而退出市场。
  - 主张通过市场竞争和技术社区的自律来解决问题，而不是依赖政府干预。
  - 担心监管机构缺乏足够的技术理解，可能制定不合理或过时的法规。

• 中立或折中观点：
  - 认为需要在监管和创新之间找到平衡，既要保护消费者，又要保持科技行业的活力。
  - 建议针对具体问题（如隐私、垄断）制定有针对性的、灵活的法规，而不是一刀切的全面监管。
  - 提出可以借鉴其他行业的监管经验，建立科技行业的自律组织或行业标准。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于监管的力度和方式，具体包括如何在保护消费者和促进创新之间取得平衡，以及监管机构的能力和角色。
• 讨论中有人提到不同国家和地区在科技监管上的差异，比如美国和欧洲的不同做法，以及这些差异对全球科技公司的影响。
• 还有人关注到监管的具体实施问题，包括如何确保法规的执行和监督，以及如何避免法规被大公司利用来打击竞争对手。

CPB to shut down after public media loses federal funding
The Corporation for Public Broadcasting, which funnels federal money to public media stations, says it's winding down operations after President Trump signed a law rescinding all funding.

By

Corporation for Public Broadcasting President and CEO Patricia de Stacy Harrison, shown here in 2017, announced on Friday that CPB would wind down operations by Sept. 30 after losing all federal funding.

The Corporation for Public Broadcasting, the conduit for federal funds to NPR and PBS, announced on Friday that it is beginning to wind down its operations given President Trump has signed a law clawing back $1.1 billion in funding for public broadcasting through fiscal year 2027.
The announcement follows a largely party-line vote last month that approved the cuts to public broadcasting as part of a
$9 billion rescissions package
requested by the White House that also included cuts to foreign aid. While public media officials had held a glimmer of hope that lawmakers would restore some of the money for the following budget year, the Senate Appropriations Committee declined to do that on Thursday.

"Despite the extraordinary efforts of millions of Americans who called, wrote, and petitioned Congress to preserve federal funding for CPB, we now face the difficult reality of closing our operations," CPB President and CEO Patricia Harrison said in a statement. "CPB remains committed to fulfilling responsibilities and supporting our partners through this transition with transparency and care."
"Public media has been one of the most trusted institutions in American life, providing educational opportunity, emergency alerts, civil discourse, and cultural connection to every corner of the country," Harrison said.
CPB informed employees that the majority of staff positions will be eliminated with the close of the fiscal year on September 30, 2025. It said a small team would remain until January to "focus on compliance, fiscal distributions, and resolution of long-term financial obligations including ensuring continuity for music rights and royalties that remain essential to the public media system," according to the CPB statement.
Media
NPR news chief announces she's leaving days after Congress kills federal funding
Harrison noted that it was the first time in nearly 60 years that Congress had refused to fund CPB. The private nonprofit corporation was set up to channel federal money to public media stations nationwide, both for programming and emergency alert systems.
Analysis
How bipartisan support for public media unraveled in the Trump era
Shock and sadness reverberated through the public media system Friday.
"I didn't really see a day where this separate institution, which is set up to serve the public, would be shut down," said Tim Bruno, general manager of Radio Catskill, an NPR affiliate in upstate New York.
"I don't know what stage of grief I'm in right now."
Earlier this summer, some stations began laying off staff in anticipation of federal funding cuts. On Wednesday, WQED — which runs a TV station and classical radio station in Pittsburgh — announced plans to lay off 35% of its staff.
Sponsor Message
Other operations, including Nashville Public Media, Louisville Public Media and KUOW in Seattle, say they are seeing a big surge in donations in response to the cuts.
Trump and his allies in Congress have argued that public media — especially NPR — is unfair to conservatives and a waste of taxpayer money. Both NPR and PBS have denied bias.
NPR, which produces news programs such as
Morning Edition
and
All Things Considered
,
relies on direct federal funds for only a small portion of its budget. But its approximately
1,000 member stations
receive a heftier portion of their operating revenue through CPB. Those in rural and poor areas in particular rely on CPB grants. With its nightly
PBS News Hour
and children's programming, such as
Daniel Tiger's Neighborhood
, PBS gets around 15% of its revenue from federal money, as do its member stations on average.
"
The ripple effects of this closure will be felt across every public media organization and, more importantly, in every community across the country that relies on public broadcasting," NPR President and CEO Katherine Maher said in
a statement
.
She said NPR would respond by "stepping up to support locally owned, nonprofit public radio stations and local journalism across the country, working to maintain public media's promise of universal service, and upholding the highest standards for independent journalism and cultural programming in service of our nation."
